Title: Idrus Harun among 4 appointed as members of Judicial Appointments Commission
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has appointed four people, including former Attorney General Tan Sri Idrus Harun, as members of the Judicial Appointments Commission for a two-year term, effective today.
Also appointed are former Federal Court Judge Tan Sri Zainun Ali; Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) law lecturer Prof Dr Hartini Saripan (for a second term); and former Sabah State Attorney General Datuk Mariati Robert.
The Office of the Secretary of the Judicial Appointments Commission, in a statement today, said the appointments were made in accordance with subsection 5(1)(f) of the Judicial Appointments Commission Act 2009.
"These appointments are for a two-year term, effective from Nov 1, 2026, to Oct 31, 2028," the statement read.
The Judicial Appointments Commission also expressed its appreciation and gratitude to Datuk Seri Talat Mahmood Abdul Rashid for his service and contributions during his tenure as a member of the Commission.

Title: Northeast monsoon: Let us strive towards zero flood-related fatalities
Article:
LETTERS:
As we enter the Northeast Monsoon season, I wish to call on all relevant authorities, disaster management agencies and communities to make ZERO FLOOD-RELATED FATALITIES our collective target and commitment.
While heavy rainfall and flooding may be unavoidable in certain circumstances, the loss of human lives should never be accepted as inevitable. We must strive to ensure zero drownings, zero preventable deaths and zero avoidable tragedies throughout this monsoon season.
Achieving this target requires a high level of preparedness, vigilance and coordination among all relevant agencies. Preparedness must be proactive rather than reactive.
Authorities must ensure that flood-prone areas are identified, drainage systems are properly maintained, evacuation centres are ready, emergency supplies are sufficient, and rescue personnel and equipment can be mobilised without delay.
Effective coordination among Nadma, the Fire and Rescue Department, police, local authorities and other relevant agencies is crucial. Early-warning systems must be strengthened, flood warnings communicated promptly, and evacuation operations carried out without hesitation whenever necessary.
Equally important is the safety and personal responsibility of the public. I wish to remind everyone:
1. Never attempt to walk, ride or drive through floodwaters, as even seemingly shallow water can be extremely dangerous.
2. Stay away from rivers, streams and waterways during heavy rainfall, as water levels and currents can change rapidly.
3. Follow evacuation instructions immediately and do not take unnecessary risks to protect property or belongings.
4. Give special attention and assistance to senior citizens, children, persons with disabilities and vulnerable individuals living in flood-prone areas.
5. Keep emergency supplies, essential medication, drinking water, flashlights and important documents ready.
6. Stay updated through official weather forecasts, flood warnings and announcements from the authorities.
We must recognise that flood preparedness is not solely the responsibility of the government and emergency responders. Every individual, family, community and business has a role to play in preventing unnecessary loss of life.
I therefore urge all authorities to treat zero flood-related fatalities not merely as an aspiration but as a serious operational commitment throughout this Northeast Monsoon season. This requires clear responsibilities, effective coordination, timely intervention and accountability at every level.
Let us learn from the tragedies and loss of life experienced during previous monsoon seasons and ensure that every possible preventive measure is taken.
Our message must be clear: Floods may be unavoidable, but preventable deaths must not be. Every life matters, and no effort should be spared to ensure that everyone remains safe throughout this monsoon season.
TAN SRI LEE LAM THYE
Alliance for a Safe Community chairman

Title: MTL, super El Nino: Malaysia faces flood and drought risks
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia faces two weather challenges in the coming months, with heavy rain and floods during the Northeast Monsoon, followed by hotter, drier conditions from a possible Super El Nino that could cause drought, water shortages and affect agriculture.
The MTL, which began on Oct 27 and is expected to continue until March 2027, is forecast to bring between three and five episodes of continuous heavy rain, particularly from this November to January next year, thereby increasing the risk of flooding, especially in low-lying areas and near rivers.
The weather developments throughout the past week has also provided an early indication when heavy rain almost every afternoon in the capital city caused several flash floods, thus disrupting traffic flow and residents' daily activities.
Flood incidents have also been reported in several states including Perak, Kedah and Negri Sembilan, indicating weather risks that need to be monitored throughout this monsoon season.
However, both phenomena do not necessarily occur sequentially or have a uniform impact across the country; instead, rainfall distribution and temperature increases are expected to vary by region and seasonal changes.
Climatology expert Professor Emeritus Datuk Dr Azizan Abu Samah said the MTL in Peninsular Malaysia typically has two main phases, with heavy rain concentrated in the East Coast such as Kelantan, Terengganu, and the northern part of Kedah between November and December, before shifting south to Johor and Sarawak in January to February.
He said the movement of the monsoon trough and monsoon surge bringing strong winds are among the factors contributing to continuous rain and increasing the risk of flooding in the area.
However, the strong influence of the El Nino has the potential to reduce the intensity and duration of rainfall throughout the MTL, particularly in November and December, thereby possibly lowering the risk of major floods like those that occurred in 2021.
Azizan also expects the number of monsoon surges to potentially decrease from the usual seven to eight to around five to six episodes, in addition to reducing the risk of large waves, coastal erosion, and sea level rise due to storm surges in coastal areas facing the South China Sea.
However, Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM) climatology and climate change expert Prof Emeritus Fredolin Tangang said that the reduction in average rainfall due to the El Nino does not mean Malaysia will be spared from floods because extreme weather events can still occur.
"Although on average the MTL weakens during a strong El Nino, this does not mean we will not face the flooding phenomena. It still needs to be monitored, we still need to be prepared," he told Bernama.
Meanwhile, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) anticipates that the Super El Nino phenomenon could bring hotter and drier conditions next year, particularly between late January and March, with maximum temperatures potentially exceeding 41 degrees Celsius.
Fredolin said the risk of hot weather and heatwaves in Peninsular Malaysia is expected to be more pronounced around March to April, while drier conditions in northern Borneo, particularly northern Sarawak and Sabah, have the potential to increase the risk of forest and peatland fires until April or May 2027.
He said the rain brought by the MTL to southern Sumatra and Kalimantan is expected to help reduce the risk of forest and peatland fires that contributes to cross-border haze before drier conditions potentially shift to northern Borneo.
Meanwhile, Azizan said the prolonged hot and dry weather also increases the risk of local haze due to open burning, including the burning of rice straw in Kedah, although the impact is expected to be more limited compared to cross-border haze.
Beyond the haze, reduced rainfall can also impact the nation's water resources – specifically the dams that supply water for domestic and agricultural use.
Azizan said the Timah Tasoh Dam in Perlis, as well as the Muda and Pedu dams in Kedah, are at risk of declining water levels should the dry conditions persist. This is particularly concerning given that the northern region of the Peninsula typically relies on rainfall during the monsoon transition period – roughly from April to May – to replenish its water reserves.
The risk of drought also places pressure on the agricultural sector, especially regarding off-season rice cultivation in the northern "rice bowl" areas of the Peninsula.
Fredolin added that a scarcity of water resources and a decline in agricultural yields could threaten food security and drive up food prices.
Furthermore, it exposes the public to risks such as heatstroke and other health issues associated with hot weather.
He emphasised that advancements in climate science should be integrated into disaster management planning; since the El Nino phenomenon can be predicted months in advance, it provides relevant authorities with the opportunity to implement preparatory measures. -BERNAMA

Title: Palestinian Agriculture Minister: malaysia can build sustainable farming partnerships
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia can turn its continued solidarity with Palestine into a sustainable partnership with Palestinian farmers by cooperating in three key areas to help the agricultural sector recover and enable farmers to earn a living from their land.
Palestinian Agriculture Minister Prof Dr Rezq Salimia said the three areas include rehabilitating damaged farms and agricultural infrastructure, strengthening cooperation between academic and agricultural institutions in both countries, and expanding market access for Palestinian products in Malaysia.
"Malaysia can turn its concern and solidarity into a sustainable partnership with Palestinian farmers.
"I welcome cooperation in three practical areas," he said in a recent interview on Bernama TV's
The Nation Diplomatic Dispatch
programme titled "Palestine Beyond the Headlines: The Battle for Land and Livelihoods."
Elaborating on the first area, Salimia said rehabilitating water systems and greenhouses, providing sustainable farming inputs and helping farmers replace damaged equipment could support agricultural recovery, including in parts of Gaza where safe access is possible.
On the second area, he proposed partnerships between universities, agricultural institutions and cooperatives in both countries through joint research, technical exchanges and training programmes to improve water efficiency, develop food processing industries and support farming projects led by women and young people.
On the third area, Salimia called for greater access for Palestinian products, particularly olive oil and dates, to the Malaysian market, stressing the need for reliable buyers, fair prices and long-term purchasing agreements to help farmers plan and invest.
"We produce more than 28,000 tonnes of dates, and we need markets like Malaysia to be open to our producing communities," he said, adding that cooperation should involve Palestinian institutions and local producers, with clear targets and transparency.
Expressing appreciation for Malaysia's continued solidarity with Palestine, Salimia said: "A sustainable partnership will enable more Palestinian families to earn a living from their land.
"This will give the solidarity that our people deeply appreciate ... real and practical strength." — BERNAMA

Title: EU's new levy on parcels kicks in
Article:
BRUSSELS, Belgium: The European Union imposed a two-euro (US$2.25) handling fee on packages from outside the 27-nation bloc on Sunday in a bid to curb the influx from China.
The new levy — introduced just weeks before the Black Friday, Cyber Monday and Christmas shopping rush — will be on top of the EU's three-euro fee on small parcels.
HOW WILL IT WORK?
The fee will apply to each type of item in a package sent directly to consumers from outside the EU, regardless of the parcel's value.
For example, if there are 10 T-shirts in a package, the handling fee will be two euros. But if a package contains two hats and 10 T-shirts, the fee will be four euros.
The handling fee comes on top of the three-euro duty imposed in July on small packages worth less than 150 euros.
European consumers are not expected to pay the handling fee, the EU insists, but online retailers and sellers can add a two-euro charge before a sale.
The European Consumer Organisation (BEUC) said it was "concerned that some platforms may try to pass these new costs onto consumers at the final stages of the purchase".
It added: "That would be illegal under EU law, which requires the full price to be shown upfront."
WHY IS THE EU INTRODUCING THE FEE?
Nearly six billion small packages entered the EU last year, according to official data.
Some 93 per cent of the cheap packages that arrived in Europe came from China, usually via popular Asian platforms such as AliExpress and Temu.
Brussels says this is putting increasing strain on customs authorities, thereby raising their costs. The handling fee will compensate for their efforts.
Since the EU imposed the three-euro duty on small parcels in July, imports have fallen by around 64 per cent — although officials warn it is too early to draw firm conclusions.
Europe has also expressed concern about "unsafe" non-EU products, such as toys that violate the bloc's rules, arriving via Chinese e-commerce platforms.
"For years customs have been asked to take on illegal imports with limited resources while small parcels have multiplied out of control," BEUC's Agustin Reyna said.
WHAT'S NEXT?
The two-euro handling fee is a permanent levy, but the three-euro duty on low-value packages is a temporary measure in place until July 1, 2028.
From that date onwards, standard, product-specific customs tariffs will apply.
The EU will have to assess the handling fee's amount every two years to ensure it remains proportional to the cost of customs operations in the bloc.

Title: Young candidate Farzana puts livelihoods, infrastructure at heart of Klebang campaign
Article:
MELAKA: Pakatan Harapan candidate for Klebang, Farzana Hayani Mohd Nasir, 26, is determined to make residents' concerns her top priority if elected.
She said several pressing issues in the constituency required attention, including recurring floods, fishermen's jetty infrastructure and efforts to empower housewives and young people economically.
"In Klebang, we have padi farmers, fishermen, youths and women. For now, I am focusing on these four key areas.
"For fishermen in Kampung Pinang, for example, we have identified problems involving the drainage system and infrastructure. We will also work on solutions for flood-prone areas such as Murni, Kampung Seberang Gajah and Bukit Rambai.
"For women and youths, our focus is on helping housewives increase their income and creating more job opportunities," she said during a walkabout at Taman Nirwana here yesterday.
Farzana acknowledged that she faced a major challenge from more experienced opponents but said she was ready to shoulder the responsibility if given the mandate.
She is also the youngest female candidate in this Melaka state election and said her experience contesting the Sungai Rambai seat in the previous state election had provided valuable lessons.
She said these would help ensure better-organised and stronger preparations by her campaign machinery this time.
"A four-cornered contest is certainly challenging, especially when I am up against seasoned politicians and am the only young female candidate in Klebang.
"But, God willing, we will work harder to win Klebang.
"As a native of Bukit Rambai, which is under the Klebang constituency, I am drawing on my previous experience to strengthen our efforts here and reach out to more voters," she said.
She said campaigning activities had begun early, with various community programmes involving mosques and surau in Klebang.
In the 2021 Melaka election, Melaka MCA chairman Datuk Lim Ban Hong won the Klebang seat with 5,028 votes, defeating PKR candidate Datuk Gue Teck, who secured 4,152 votes, and Perikatan Nasional's Bakri Jamaluddin, who garnered 3,884 votes.

Title: Canada advancing its 'middle power' strategy with new trade deals, Anand says
Article:
ATLANTA: Canada is making rapid progress in diversifying its trade and security ties globally, with a goal of doubling its non-US trade over the next decade, Foreign Minister Anita Anand said on Saturday, as Ottawa emphasises trust in building new relationships outside North America.
Anand spoke with Reuters on the sidelines of a US-hosted meeting of foreign ministers from the Group of 20 major economies, where the participation of Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov exposed deep divisions within the grouping.
A critic of Lavrov's participation, Anand said the meeting helped illustrate the transformed and fractured nature of the international order, underscoring the need for new approaches, groupings, alliances and partnerships.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has vowed to double Canada's non-US trade over the next decade as President Donald Trump's tariffs have rippled through the Canadian economy.
Canada's subsequent efforts to reach a deal with Washington have broken down, prompting Carney's government to aggressively pursue trade pacts with countries across the Asia-Pacific, Europe and the Middle East.
"This is our middle power diplomacy," Anand told Reuters, citing Canada's work with Nordic countries on Arctic safety and security amid growing Russian threats, as well as efforts with India and Australia to protect citizens' privacy amid rapid advances in AI and innovation.
Canada was also working to expand its ties with the European Union, she said, citing a new national security strategy released earlier in the week that places significant emphasis on critical minerals, energy and food security.
"Canada is coming to the table to ensure that ... there are, if necessary, new bodies, new groupings, new alliances and partnerships in order to address the crises of the day," she said.
Ottawa had forged 20 new security and trade agreements with countries and parties worldwide, giving it access to 1.50 billion consumers in more than 51 countries, and efforts to expand trade ties outside the US would continue.
She said Canada was the only Group of Seven country with free trade agreements with every other G7 member, and expected to conclude a similar trade deal with Asean before the end of the year.

Title: China's new ambassador to Malaysia prioritises trade, AI and semiconductors
Article:
SEPANG: China's newly appointed  Ambassador to Malaysia Yao Wen has pledged to further strengthen bilateral relations, with greater emphasis on economic cooperation, emerging technologies and people-to-people exchanges.
In his written address upon arriving at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) yesterday, Yao said his key priorities included translating the consensus reached by leaders of both countries into concrete actions and advancing cooperation in areas such as infrastructure, trade, Artificial Intelligence (AI) and semiconductors.
"It is a great pleasure to be back in Malaysia, a beautiful country known as 'Malaysia, Truly Asia', as I step into my new role. After years working in the region and visiting Malaysia numerous times, I have always held a special place for this country in my heart.
"My ultimate goal is to advance all-dimensional cooperation and friendly exchanges, fostering an even closer bond between our two peoples. To this end, I look forward to working hand in hand with our Malaysian friends to pursue four key priorities," he said.
Yao, 53, arrived from Beijing on Saturday night via an Air China flight, succeeding Ouyang Yujing as China's ambassador to Malaysia. He was received by representatives from the Foreign Ministry's Protocol and Consular Department.
As the first priority, Yao said both countries should strengthen political mutual trust and consolidate their longstanding friendship.
He said China was advancing its national rejuvenation through Chinese modernisation, while Malaysia was making strategic progress under the Malaysia Madani vision.
He said the two countries were well positioned to support each other's modernisation efforts, deepen strategic mutual trust and ensure the steady, long-term development of their high-level strategic community with a shared future.
On economic cooperation, Yao said both countries should advance the high-quality development of the Belt and Road Initiative, strengthening cooperation in traditional sectors such as infrastructure and trade while exploring new opportunities in AI and semiconductors.
On the third priority, he called for deeper people-to-people exchanges, describing close ties between the peoples of both countries as the foundation of sound bilateral relations.
"Both countries should leverage their mutual visa-free policy and the opportunity presented by Visit Malaysia Year 2026 to strengthen cooperation in education, culture, healthcare, tourism and exchanges at the sub-national level," he added.
He also expressed hope for the successful hosting of the Confucian-Islamic Civilisational Dialogues to further promote mutual understanding and bring the peoples of both countries closer.
On the fourth priority, Yao called for stronger multilateral coordination between Malaysia and China to promote international fairness and justice.
"Together, China and Malaysia must uphold the international system with the United Nations at its core, champion international fairness and justice, and amplify the voice of the Global South to forge a more equitable global governance system.
"By staying committed to openness and development, and pioneering rules for emerging domains, we can inject much-needed certainty into a world fraught with turbulence and volatility."
Yao said he was committed to building on the legacy of his predecessors and working closely with Malaysians from all walks of life to deepen comprehensive cooperation and strengthen the longstanding friendship between the two countries.
He said both sides should continue fostering dialogue, sharing insights and pooling their wisdom to strengthen bilateral ties and bring enduring prosperity to their peoples for generations to come.

Title: RM30mil media fund to support digitalisation, safeguard media jobs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Media Innovation Fund 2.0 reflects the government's continued commitment to ensuring the sustainability of local media companies and preventing retrenchments amid industry headwinds.
Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama) chief executive officer Datin Paduka Nur-ul Afida Kamaludin said the initiative would help news organisations procure up-to-date tools and equipment to bolster their platforms and develop fresh revenue streams.
"The Media Innovation Fund is not merely financial assistance for media organisations; it serves as a strategic government investment to secure the future of the nation's journalism industry.
"This initiative enables media organisations like Bernama to strengthen their technological capabilities, develop talent and produce quality content, all without compromising ethical principles, integrity or journalistic freedom," she said here today.
Nur-ul Afida said Bernama welcomed the continuation of the fund and intended to apply for new equipment across its 14 bureaus nationwide.
She said the move aligned with Bernama's plans to reinforce its artificial intelligence (AI)-driven newsroom, upskill personnel and accelerate digital transformation.
"We hope that media companies will make optimal use of this fund to build a Malaysian media industry that is more innovative, competitive and sustainable in the long term," she said.
Nur-ul Afida also welcomed the introduction of a new funding scope for news service and media content subscriptions, noting it aligned with Bernama's mandate as the national news agency and primary content provider for domestic media outlets.
She said the category likely stemmed from feedback gathered during a media dialogue organised by the Malaysian Media Council in conjunction with National Journalists' Day (Hawana) in June.
"Therefore, I encourage media companies to apply for this segment, which is designed to alleviate the financial burden of covering news service subscription costs," she said.
Last Friday, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil announced a RM30 million allocation under the Media Innovation Fund 2.0 to
empower
the local media industry through digitalisation, talent development and the adoption of emerging technologies such as AI.
He said the programme built on the original Media Innovation Fund announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in conjunction with Hawana.
The fund covers five areas: media personnel training; software and technology adoption; equipment, hardware and supporting facilities; research and content development; and subscriptions to news services and media content.
Media companies receiving the grant are barred from carrying out arbitrary staff retrenchments, even when facing financial constraints.
Applications are open until Nov 14 via the official portal at https://danainovasimedia.komunikasi.gov.my/.

Title: Spanish village holds memorial Mass for 69 train crash victims
Article:
URDA: Residents and local officials gathered on Saturday in a Spanish village near the site of a high-speed train collision that killed at least 69 people for a memorial Mass honouring the victims.
The pews inside the San Juan Bautista church in Urda, in the central province of Toledo, were packed, while dozens more people gathered outside to listen to the service. Some wiped away tears.
Investigators are looking into the cause of one of Europe's deadliest rail disasters this century, which occurred when a train travelling from Madrid to Seville crashed into a stationary train on Wednesday.
Archbishop of Toledo Francisco Cerro acknowledged that "there are no words that can offer comfort" to those who had lost loved ones.
But he added: "Dear families affected by the train accident, you are not alone. Society is with you, the best of society is with you."
He urged the public not to forget the tragedy, calling for such disasters never to happen again.
He also paid tribute to emergency service workers and volunteers, praising what he described as "a genuine wave of solidarity."
The president of the Castilla-La Mancha region, Emiliano Garcia-Page, and Urda mayor Manuel Galan were among those attending the service.
- 'IN GREAT PAIN' -
Residents of Urda, which has a population of around 2,500, "are very badly affected, in great pain and with a great need for support", Galan told Spanish public television ahead of the mass.
Village pharmacist, 78-year-old Antonio Garcia Colina, said he had rushed to the scene of the crash in his car shortly after it happened to try to help the injured and witnessed several people dying.
"As I walked toward the scene of the disaster, toward ground zero, I started seeing that the passengers were in bad shape as they were being pulled out of the train cars,"  he told AFPTV, describing the scene as "hellish."
Relatives of the victims, who have been providing DNA samples to help identify the dead, face an agonising wait for news as rescue teams continue to sift through the wreckage and forensic experts work to identify the bodies.
Authorities overseeing the process have completed autopsies on all 69 people killed in the crash, with 56 identified so far, according to their latest update.
Of those identified, 54 were Spanish nationals and two were foreign nationals – one French and the other Portuguese.
Wednesday's crash was Spain's second major train disaster this year.
In January, 46 people were killed when one train derailed and slammed into the side of another travelling in the opposite direction on the same route, near the southern village of Adamuz.--AFP

Title: Bursa Malaysia expected to consolidate next week, trade within 1,600-1,630 level
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia is expected to consolidate next week, with the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) projected to trade within the 1,600-1,630 range amid a mildly positive bias.
Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said the outlook remains cautiously optimistic, with selective bargain hunting for fundamentally sound blue-chip stocks expected to support the local market.
"The benchmark index has demonstrated resilience around 1,600 this week, although a sustained move above the 1,620 level may prove challenging without stronger buying participation.
"Next week, investors will also monitor Bank Negara Malaysia's monetary policy decision on Nov 5 and upcoming corporate earnings," he told Bernama.
Meanwhile, IPPFA Director of Investment Strategy and Country Economist Mohd Sedek Jantan said  Malaysia's Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI), scheduled for release on Nov 2, will be an important indicator of underlying economic momentum.
He said the previous month's reading slipped below the 50-point threshold, signalling a contraction in manufacturing activity.
"A further deterioration could raise concerns over the resilience of the manufacturing sector, particularly against the backdrop of higher energy costs and external uncertainties.
"Conversely, an improvement in the PMI could reinforce confidence in domestic economic fundamentals and provide support for local equities," said Mohd Sedek.
On a Friday-to-Friday basis, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) increased 4.04 points to 1,615.60 from 1,611.56 a week ago.
On the index board, the FBM Emas Index added 68.28 points to 12,061.73, the FBM Top 100 Index increased 66.25 points to 11,863.86, and the FBM Emas Shariah Index garnered 139.34 points to 12,082.91.
The FBM ACE Index rose 57.77 points to 5,403.91, and the FBM Mid 70 Index went up 250.36 points to 17,420.69.
By sector, the Energy Index advanced 17.49 points to 852.16, the Plantation Index gained 19.94 points to 8,697.42, and the Industrial Products and Services Index climbed 2.97 points to 178.37. The Financial Services Index tumbled 106.33 points to 18,547.99.
Weekly turnover increased to 15.53 billion units worth RM9.97 billion from 14.21 billion units worth RM12.55 billion in the previous week.
However, the Main Market volume fell to 5.13 billion units valued at RM8.83 billion versus 7.68 billion units valued at RM11.15 billion previously.
Warrants turnover decreased to 3.99 billion units worth RM608.01 million against 4.15 billion units worth RM514.80 million a week ago.
The ACE Market volume slid to 2.07 billion units valued at RM788.72 million from 2.37 billion units valued at RM889.53 million in the previous week.

Title: South Korea exports nearly double in October, strongest growth since 1974
Article:
SEOUL: South Korea's exports nearly doubled in October from a year earlier, beating market expectations and marking the sharpest increase in more than 50 years, trade data showed on Sunday.
Exports from Asia's fourth-largest economy, a bellwether for global trade, rose 93.70 per cent last month to US$115.28 billion, slightly higher than the median forecast of a 93.20 per cent increase in a Reuters poll of economists.
The increase, boosted by favourable calendar effects from more working days due to differences in the timing of local Chuseok holidays, exceeded September's 83.70 per cent gain and was the strongest since January 1974.
Overseas sales of semiconductors jumped 259.40 per cent as prices and volumes remained high amid continued facility investment by global big tech firms competing for leadership in the artificial intelligence industry, the trade ministry said.
Computer sales surged 496.60 per cent on increasing server demand for AI services.
Imports rose 36.00 per cent to US$72.78 billion, following a 26.00 per cent increase in September, marking the biggest annual rise since January 2022.
The country's monthly trade balance recorded a surplus of US$42.50 billion, narrower than the record US$49.97 billion surplus in the previous month.

Title: Iran warns US, Israel against new attacks after Trump, Netanyahu threats
Article:
TEHERAN: Iran's supreme leader warned the United States and Israel Saturday of fresh attacks following their threats to resume strikes after crucial elections, as fears increased over a return to fighting.
President Donald Trump suggested he could launch fresh military action after the United States holds its midterm elections early next week.
But US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Saturday: "If there is a diplomatic solution, we would be open to it."
In Israel, which is coming off a general election, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has spoken of a "historic, one-time opportunity" to topple the Iranian government.
The elections in both countries could determine the direction of the conflict, with Israel having voted on Tuesday but yet to form a new government.
"Any level or type of threat must be met with an immediate, impactful and geographically unrestricted response," Iran's supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei told top military commanders, according to a statement.
Khamenei also ordered commanders to update Iran's target list to include "all types of tangible and intangible assets belonging to the American-Zionist enemy."
Iran has previously warned it would consider severing undersea cables in the Strait of Hormuz.
This was the first reported meeting between Khamenei and military top brass.
The supreme leader has not been seen publicly since before he took the helm in March, after the killing of his father Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in US-Israeli strikes.
- OIL PRICE SPIKE -
Rubio warned that "we can achieve military objectives if we seek to", adding that Trump had not made a decision on any fresh strikes.
Since the initial US-Israeli bombardment in February, ordinary Iranians "have been left in a state of limbo for the past year", Fariba, a Teheran housewife, told AFP.
But other residents in the Iranian capital brushed off the possible return to full-scale conflict.
"We do not fear another war," said Ebrahim, a salesman in his forties. "We have been at war for 48 years now."
Since the outbreak of the war, Teheran has restricted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, which normally carries around one-fifth of global oil consumption.
A ship traversing the strait struck a mine and caught fire, Iranian state television reported Saturday.
On Friday, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said three oil tankers had been halted after encountering unspecified "incidents" or hitting mines.
The blockade has caused a spike in global energy prices, making the war unpopular among the US public ahead of midterm congressional elections Tuesday.
Gains for the opposition Democrats could restrict, to an extent, Trump's ability to enact policy.
Voting in Israel has left Netanyahu's political camp with the most seats in parliament but short of a majority, leaving the make-up of the next administration unclear.
- 'FLAMES OF WAR' -
The war began on Feb 28 with US-Israeli strikes on Iran. The Islamic republic swiftly responded with attacks on American assets in countries around the region.
Fresh diplomatic efforts are underway to avert any resumption of fighting.
Qatari mediators landed in Teheran on Friday, and US Vice President JD Vance sent a letter to Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei.
"I read the letter," said Rezaei, head of Iran's supreme national security council, in a video broadcast on Iranian television.
"I haven't yet responded. Their tone has completely changed," he added, describing that as "a good sign."
But he declined to comment further on its contents.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said there were currently no plans for meetings with US officials.
"Iran's conditions are clear, and consultations regarding them are ongoing among mediators," he said in an interview with Al Jazeera, according to the state news agency IRNA.
- 'RED LINES' WARNING -
Rezaei insisted Iran would continue to blockade the Strait of Hormuz until its conditions, including releasing frozen assets, were met.
"We want the war to end in such a way that no one dares to attack Iran anymore," he added.
Qatar and Pakistan have been mediating between the warring parties, but the talks have yet to produce a lasting agreement.
The Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday that Vance had sent his letter to Iran's security chief at Trump's direction to try to revive negotiations and avert further US strikes.
The Iranian side kept its firm warnings against further attacks Saturday.
Army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia said any resumption of hostilities would only expand the scope of the war.
"The flames of war will undoubtedly engulf a much wider geographical area," he said on social media.
Araghchi warned on X that there would no longer be any "red lines."--AFP

Title: Ringgit expected to trade in narrow range vs greenback ahead of BNM's OPR decision

Title: Public Service Dept allocates RM1.46m to upgrade village, school
Article:
GOPENG: THE Public Service Department (PSD) has allocated RM1.465 million for physical improvement and community projects under the Kampung Angkat Madani and Sekolah Angkat Madani programmes.
The initiative benefits Kampung Kota Bharu in Kampar and SMK Malim Nawar, with eight of nine planned physical projects completed.
The projects include upgrading Masjid Jamek Kota Bharu , the community hall, health clinic, police station and primary school facilities.
A landmark featuring artwork by renowned cartoonist Datuk Lat, who hails from the village, was also built under the initiative.
In addition, 11 community programmes were organised, including a 'korban' programme, fishing competition, traditional sports activities and a public religious lecture.
The programmes aim to strengthen human capital development and improve the well-being of the community.
Public Service director-general  Tan Sri Dr Wan Ahmad Dahlan Abdul Aziz said the programme, which began in April, demonstrated how strategic cooperation between government agencies could translate plans into tangible benefits for the people.
"This is how we put the Malaysia Madani concept into practice. Government officers go to the ground to identify residents' needs and provide assistance accordingly.
"PSD's involvement will not end here. Although the programme has concluded, we will continue monitoring the projects and maintaining contact with villagers.
"This is to ensure the infrastructure provided is properly maintained."
He said this after officiating at the closing of the PSD's Kampung Angkat Madani and Sekolah Angkat Madani programmes at SK Kota Baharu's field here yesterday.
Present were Association of Wives and Women Members of the Malaysian Civil Service (Puspanita) PSD branch chairman Puan Sri
Dr Azlifah Bahari and Perak State Financial Officer Datuk Mohd Zaki Mahyudin.
At the ceremony, Rahmah food baskets were distributed to 97 families in Kampung Kota Bharu. Contributions were also presented to the school, while strategic partners received tokens of appreciation.
Wan Ahmad Dahlan said community engagement activities allowed public officers to better understand the realities faced by residents.
He added that meaningful relationships could be built when initiatives were designed around the actual needs of communities.
"Ultimately, Madani development is not merely about building infrastructure, but also nurturing the potential and well-being of the people."
He said RM500,000 allocated by the Finance Ministry and RM35,000 from PSD were used to implement eight physical projects.
Two additional physical projects were carried out in collaboration with the Rural and Regional Development Ministry, including the installation of 40 solar-powered street lights worth RM380,000.
The Implementation Coordination Unit of the Prime Minister's Department also allocated RM450,000 for a new multipurpose hall.
The facility, which is still under construction, will accommodate two badminton courts.
Under the Sekolah Angkat Madani initiative, RM90,000 was allocated to SMK Malim Nawar to upgrade its computer laboratory, design and technology workshop and science laboratory.
A further RM10,000 was channelled towards educational development programmes for students and teachers.
Wan Ahmad Dahlan said seven high-impact programmes were also organised for students, including the Knowledge Camp, Student Excellence and Character Development programme, benchmarking visits and uniformed unit camps.
Teachers were also included in initiatives like the School Leadership Professionalism programme, Guru Madani engagement sessions and the Legal Literacy programme.
He said Kampung Kota Bharu was selected as PSD's adopted village after assessments found that several of its basic facilities lagged behind those in other areas.
However, the village was found to have considerable development potential.
"We identified the potential of this village. Today, we can see that many of its facilities have been upgraded, all for the benefit of the community," Wan Ahmad Dahlan said.
"As for the adopted school,
we found that students at SMK
Malim Nawar had limited exposure to opportunities beyond their immediate surroundings.
"So we brought them to places such as Putrajaya and Cyberjaya to broaden their horizons and expose them to the wider world.
"These experiences have given them new perspectives and will hopefully motivate them to strive for greater achievements."
He also praised SK Kota Baharu's team for winning a gold medal with its Ecowire Roll innovation at the International Innovation and Entrepreneurship Expo 2026 on Oct 25.
He also highlighted the achievement of a student from SMK Malim Nawar who represented Selangor in football.
Wan Ahmad Dahlan said the achievements showed that rural students could excel when given the right opportunities, facilities and support.
"They, too, can turn their ideas into reality. This shows that schools in rural areas have the potential to achieve recognition at a higher level."

Title: FBI blames North Korea for US$6.34b Binance crypto heist
Article:
NEW YORK: The FBI on Saturday accused North Korea of stealing more than US$6 billion in virtual assets from the cryptocurrency exchange Binance in what is thought to be the biggest-ever crypto heist.
The US law enforcement agency's statement came as Binance offered reassurances it was covering the losses from the hacking attack, saying it has used company funds to buy tokens to replenish 90 per cent of what was stolen.
Binance is the world's largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes. News of the cyberattack caused the prices of most major cryptocurrencies to fall sharply on Friday.
The FBI confirmed earlier suspicions from private investigators and analysts that a North Korea-affiliated group called TraderTraitor was behind the hack.
TraderTraitor is the same group blamed for a US$1.5 billion theft from the Bybit platform in February last year.
"The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) is releasing information advising the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (North Korea) was responsible for the theft of more than US$6 billion USD in virtual assets from cryptocurrency exchange Binance, on or about Oct 29, 2026," the statement said.
The FBI added that it had observed "TraderTraitor actors" converting stolen assets into Ethereum, and expected those assets to be laundered further by converting them using decentralised finance and instant swap services.
It said it was urging private sector entities "to block transactions with or derived from addresses TraderTraitor actors are using to launder these stolen assets."
- 'COVER THE FINANCIAL IMPACT' -
Binance said Saturday it has set aside more than US$6.34 billion in company funds to cover losses in the hack.
"Our commitment remains the same: Binance will fully cover the financial impact of the funds stolen in this incident," the company said on X.
It said it has used company money to buy tokens to replenish 90 per cent of the stolen funds, while the remaining 10 per cent of tokens are "less liquid, which means they may take longer to source in the required amounts."
Binance suspended user withdrawals after the hack, but said in its latest update they were on track to resume Sunday.
The attack on Binance came as many observers express worries that the ever-expanding capabilities of artificial intelligence models could compromise cryptography and IT security protocols.
Bitcoin plunged nearly five percent after the news of the hack, while Ethereum dropped nearly six per cent and BNB, native to Binance, tumbled nearly 10 per cent.
Binance said Friday it was working to resolve what it called a "complex attack" with several "points of breach."
The sheer scale of the hack has put a spotlight on the capacity of North Korea – which faces extensive international sanctions over its nuclear and missile programs – to find illicit means to capture revenue.
TraderTraitor is believed to be part of the Lazarus Group, which gained notoriety in 2014 when it was accused of hacking into Sony Pictures as revenge for "The Interview," a film that mocked North Korean leader Kim Jong Un.--AFP

Title: Myanmar begins releasing Rakhine returnees from Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:  Myanmar's military authorities have begun releasing ethnic Rakhine nationals repatriated from Malaysia after Kuala Lumpur sought clarification over their reported detention.
The Irrawaddy reported on Oct 29 the releases began two days after Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan addressed questions in Parliament about the returnees' situation.
Citing the Khamee Youth Unity Association and testimony from a released individual, the report said detainees with identification documents were being allowed to return home.
"My younger brother was only set free yesterday," a Khamee man, who requested anonymity over security concerns, told The Irrawaddy.
"I didn't even know he was among those released," he said, adding that his brother was freed after the family submitted the required documentation.
The Irrawaddy reported that more than 400 ethnic Rakhine were among nearly 1,500 Myanmar nationals repatriated from Malaysia in late September.
While other returnees were allowed to go home upon arrival, the ethnic Rakhine were reportedly held for questioning at military detention facilities in Yangon's Thanlyin and Hlaingthayar townships.
The association said 26 Khamee individuals were among those detained.
On Oct 26, Mohamad told the Dewan Rakyat that Malaysia would seek clarification from
Myanmar over allegations
that about 300 returnees remained in military detention, and instruct its chargé d'affaires to investigate their condition.
Mohamad said the repatriation was voluntary and that Myanmar had given assurances regarding the returnees' safety. The programme envisaged returning 5,000 Myanmar nationals in stages.
On Sept 29,
Malaysia repatriated
1,476 Myanmar nationals comprising 1,370 men, 79 women, and 27 children transferred from 14 immigration detention depots aboard three Myanmar naval vessels, including a hospital ship.
Myanmar has been engulfed in conflict since the military seized power in 2021. The United Nations and rights groups have warned that prevailing conditions do not guarantee safe returns.

Title: #NSTviral: Chinese teen wins praise for graceful Zapin performance
Article:
Aza Jemima Ahmad
KUALA LUMPUR: A
Malaysian Chinese teenager
has won praise online for his graceful performance of the traditional Malay dance Zapin.
Eric Tan Zhen Long, 14, a student of SMK Sri Muar in Johor, caught attention after a video of the performance was shared on Threads by the group's choreographer, Mohamad Eddy Hafifi Chuai.
Speaking to the New Straits Times, Eddy said Tan had no professional dance experience before taking up the art in 2025.
The troupe, Arunika Nidera Tari, won first place and Best Choreography in the secondary school category at Festival Zapin Jauhar 2026 in Iskandar Puteri on Oct 29.
Eddy said Tan was also named Best Male Dancer at the national-level Malaysian Schools Dance Competition, organised by the Education Ministry in June.
Established in 2024, the group comprises Malay, Chinese and Indian students.
"The dancers regularly attend Zapin workshops and undergo training at school," Eddy said.
The Threads post has since garnered more than 109,000 views, with viewers praising the dancers' skills and the performance's ability to bring people together.
"It's an annual event, right? It can be included in the tourism attraction calendar! Good job, everyone!" user nourcharme wrote.
User lolarose_19 said she had not realised Zapin could be so engaging, praising the dancers for taking pride in their performance.
Another user praised Tan's graceful movements, saying Johor's cultural identity was evident in his performance.
"I'm getting goosebumps. Art brings us together," another commenter wrote.
Zapin is a traditional Malay dance characterised by rhythmic footwork and graceful movements, accompanied by lively music played on instruments such as the gambus, a type of lute, accordion and rebana, a frame drum.
User melazayn28, who watched the performance live, said: "I watched it live yesterday. So impressive. Good job, guys."

Title: Judge dismisses Trump's US$10b lawsuit against Wall Street Journal over Epstein letter
Article:
WASHINGTON: A US judge on Saturday dismissed President Donald Trump's defamation lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal and media magnate Rupert Murdoch over a report that Trump sent a bawdy birthday letter to notorious sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
Trump had sued for US$10 billion after the newspaper's story was published in July 2025 detailing the president's alleged 2003 letter to Epstein, which apparently featured a drawing of a naked woman.
Murdoch is the founder of News Corp. which owns the Wall Street Journal.
The report piled scrutiny on Trump from both Democrats and his own Republican party, who rejected the president's attempts to downplay the saga as a hoax and called for a full release of legal files on Epstein.
In Saturday's ruling, Judge Darrin Gayles dismissed Trump's lawsuit with prejudice, meaning Trump cannot file an amended version of the suit, as he did when Gayles turned down an initial version of it back in April.
The judge wrote that in bringing his defamation claim, Trump had both times failed to establish that the defendants "acted with actual malice."
The House Oversight Committee last year published a copy of Trump's alleged birthday note to Epstein, which consists of a short dialogue between "Donald" and "Jeffrey."
"We have certain things in common," says Donald, to which Jeffrey responds: "Yes, we do, come to think of it."
"Enigmas never age, have you noticed that?" asks Donald.
"As a matter of fact, it was clear to me the last time I saw you," says Jeffrey.
"A pal is a wonderful thing. Happy Birthday – and may every day be another wonderful secret," the note ends, followed by Trump's signature, which takes the place of pubic hair on the nude outline.
- EPSTEIN FILES -
Trump's supporters have been obsessed with the Epstein case for years and held as an article of faith that "deep state" elites were protecting a sex ring of Epstein associates, particularly in the Democratic Party and Hollywood.
The president fought for months to prevent the Department of Justice from releasing the so-called "Epstein Files" but eventually signed a law passed by Congress requiring their publication.
Trump's name appears repeatedly in the documents but he denies any wrongdoing and has not been charged with any criminal offenses connected to the affair.
High-profile figures including Britain's former prince Andrew have been publicly disgraced for their associations with Epstein.
Ahead of the Nov 3 US midterm elections which will decide control of Congress, Democrats have reportedly spent more than US$35 million on Epstein-related advertisements.
With a Republican majority in the House and Senate, Trump has so far enjoyed relatively little political opposition since taking office in January 2025, giving the courts a key role in limiting him.
In a separate case Saturday, a new suit was filed to prevent Trump's attempt to erect a huge triumphal arch in front of the iconic military cemetery outside Washington.
That is one of a number of projects launched by Trump in a bid to put his personal stamp on the capital, including a ballroom at the White House and a laborious renovation of the Reflecting Pool on the National Mall.--AFP

Title: Smart sharpens flood-rescue skills ahead of northeast monsoon [WATCH]
Article:
SEPANG: Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (Smart) personnel recently honed their flood-rescue skills in a five-day exercise ahead of the northeast monsoon.
The exercise focused on operational readiness, boat handling and safe evacuations.
The Boat Handling and Water Rescue Training programme ran from Oct 19 to 23 at the Pantai Bagan Lalang General Operations Force post.
Commander Abdul Manaf Che Isa said the exercise involved 136 Smart and National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) personnel, helping them get familiar with the equipment, procedures and conditions.
The exercise followed the launch of the National Preparedness Month on Oct 11, officiated by Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
[[nid:1567977]]
"We want to ensure everyone is prepared and the assets are ready to be mobilised when floods strike several states in the peninsula, as well as Sabah and Sarawak," Manaf said.
"We are already trained in boat handling, the use of surface rescue equipment and specialised underwater rescue equipment. The aim of this training is to prepare and hone their skills."
He said the team was also trained to handle emergencies during rescue operations, such as technical issues involving boats.
New Straits Times reporters who took part in the exercise on Oct 22 saw participants practising throwing and hauling in throw bags, as well as using rope rescue devices to pull people out of the water to simulate a rescue.
They also rode in the boats as crews manoeuvred through the waves and whirlpools in choppy seas and hazy meteorological conditions.
[[nid:1567976]]
The daily schedule included boat and engine maintenance, defensive and aggressive swimming, self-rescue and capsize recovery, tactical navigation and docking, as well as boat pickup, triage and CPR on board.
Each day ended with a full simulation of a northeast monsoon flood operation.
Manaf said the training was held at sea to familiarise crews with currents, waves and calm waters, and was conducted during the day and at night to prepare them for different operational conditions.
Five aluminium boats and surface safety equipment were used.
Satellite phones and Broadband Global Area Network equipment were also brought along for use in areas without communications coverage.
Manaf said underwater rescue training would follow at a suitable location.
On Smart's role in floods, he added that it served as a support force for frontliners.
Nadma has assigned officers to zones.
Before floods arrive, Smart would deploy to key forward operating bases, where fire, civil defence, police and army responders are stationed.
Manaf said Smart was mobilised every year and its rescue operations with other agencies had gone well.
The main constraint was victims who refused to move early despite evacuation warnings.
Once flood warnings are issued, the team approaches every household to advise residents to move to relief centres.
He urged the public to prepare early, including by securing important documents and medicine for those requiring follow-up treatment.

Title: Kota Baru's forgotten flavours take centre stage in Unesco bid
Article:
KOTA BARU: For the past four months, a group of 20 friends have been spending their days off combing the state capital's wet markets, seeking out veteran traders and elderly residents who hold the recipes, memories and stories behind Kelantan's lesser-known culinary treasures.
Their search goes beyond a shared love of food; it is part of an ambitious effort to put Kota Baru on the world gastronomic map.
For the Kota Baru Gastronomy Club, the mission is to bring the state's rich culinary heritage out of the shadows and into the international spotlight, with the ultimate goal of securing a place on the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation's (Unesco) Creative Cities Network.
While nasi kerabu and laksam have long found their way beyond Kelantan's borders, the club is turning its attention to delicacies such as itik solo, kuih pinang kontang and che banding — dishes that have yet to enjoy the same recognition.
These are among more than 1,000 traditional Kelantanese dishes the club is painstakingly researching and cataloguing as part of its bid to have Kota Baru designated a Unesco Creative City of Gastronomy next year.
"We want to highlight Kota Baru and introduce the uniqueness of Kelantanese cuisine to people beyond the state, including the international community," club founder Ariza Mohd Yusoff told the New Straits Times.
Ariza said preparations for the nomination were almost 80 per cent complete, ahead of the opening of nominations in early 2027.
[[nid:1567913]]
The club has also enlisted the support of the Malaysian Association of Hotels Kelantan chapter, with several hotel chefs agreeing to lend their expertise to the effort.
The initiative received backing from the state government's Economic Planning Unit and the Kota Baru Municipal Council.
However, securing international recognition will require more than assembling an impressive collection of recipes.
Ariza said the nomination would involve comprehensive documentation of Kelantan's culinary heritage, tracing the history, cultural significance and traditional preparation methods of each dish, along with the stories behind them.
Beyond reviving interest in lesser-known delicacies, the club also hopes to showcase the diversity of familiar favourites such as nasi kerabu, including its yellow and black varieties.
"Food is not merely about eating. It is a medium that connects people and countries. We have seen how nasi kerabu has gained international exposure, including in Switzerland, and we want to build on that," Ariza said.
For her, Unesco recognition could open doors well beyond the kitchen, drawing international visitors here while creating new opportunities for local food entrepreneurs and communities.
The club also hopes to establish a recognition programme for restaurants that champion and preserve traditional Kelantanese cuisine.
The road to recognition, however, may not be without competition.
Ariza said Penang was also reportedly eyeing a nomination for George Town under the Creative City of Gastronomy category.
[[nid:1567911]]
For now, Kuching remains Malaysia's only Unesco Creative City of Gastronomy, having earned the status in 2021.
Pertubuhan Cakna Warisan dan Komuniti Malaysia chairman Johan Ariff Ismail said Kota Baru's bid was timely, given Kelantan's wealth of culinary traditions and cultural influences.
He described the state as the cradle of Malay culture, where centuries of history and the ingenuity of its people have produced a remarkable repertoire of traditional dishes, savoury delicacies and desserts.
The Universiti Teknologi Mara Kelantan adjunct professor said the state's proximity to Thailand, coupled with its historical links to Sumatra, Riau-Lingga and Champa, had left a distinct imprint on its culinary identity.
"Kelantan's gastronomy is not just about the variety of food, but also the assimilation and curation of different cultural influences."
Among the traditional delicacies deserving a wider international audience, he said, were lompat tikam, cermin molek, akok, jala mas and buah tanjung.
"When tourists visit a destination, food is often one of the main attractions. Kelantanese food reflects the state's culture, arts and heritage.
"The economic benefits would trickle down to the communities, including those who prepare traditional kuih and preserve recipes passed down through generations."
Johan said the benefits of Unesco recognition could ripple far beyond Kota Baru, reaching communities across Kelantan's 12 districts through increased tourism, business opportunities and international exposure.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: All eyes on Melaka as 79 candidates vie for 28 seats [WATCH]
Article:
MELAKA: All eyes will be on Melaka over the next 14 days as 79 candidates  enter the fray for the 28 seats up for grabs in the state election.
The battle lines became clearer yesterday  after the close of nominations, but not before  coalitions and parties made a series of last-minute adjustments to their seat allocations and candidate line-ups.
One of the surprises was Bersatu's decision to drop out of the Gadek race, despite having earlier announced its candidate for the seat.
With Bersatu out of the picture, Gadek, one of the five seats under the Alor Gajah parliamentary constituency, is now a four-cornered contest. Barisan Nasional is fielding Melaka MIC deputy chairman S. Nadarajah to defend the seat against three challengers.
They are Jegasilan Kungamboo of Pakatan Harapan, B. Laveen of Bersama and Laila Norinda Maon of Putra.
The
New Straits Times
has reached out to Bersatu secretary-general Datuk Seri Azmin Ali for comment.
A day before nomination day, MCA announced  it would contest in Kota Laksamana, adding it to the three seats the party had previously been allocated.
The Nov 14 election is also a less crowded affair than the 2021 polls, which saw 112 candidates contest the 28 seats.
Universiti Malaya political analyst Dr Mohammad Tawfik Yaakub said the situation reflected a shift towards strategic electoral cooperation and selective seat allocation.
"Political parties are increasingly concentrating their resources and grassroots machinery on constituencies where they intend to compete," he said.
"Although smaller parties remain involved, the growing number of straight fights suggests that Melaka's electoral landscape is becoming more structured around major political coalitions."
Of the 28 seats, 11 will see straight fights, with nine featuring contests between BN and PH and the remaining two between BN and Bersatu. All 11  were won by BN in  2021.
One of the key contests is in Tanjung Bidara, where caretaker Chief Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh will face PH candidate Mohd Yunazri Mustamiri. In 2021, the Melaka BN chief won the seat with a majority of 364 votes, polling 3,559 votes in a three-cornered contest.
[[nid:1568029]]
Another key BN-PH battleground is Merlimau, where Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh is defending the seat against PH candidate and state Amanah Wanita chief Rahayu Hamzah. Dr Akmal won the seat with a majority of 3,248 votes last time round.
Other seats seeing straight fights between the two coalitions, which are aligned at the federal level, are Ayer Limau, Taboh Naning, Durian Tunggal, Asahan, Ayer Molek, Duyong and Rim.
[[nid:1568028]]
Another 11 seats will see three-cornered contests, while six, including Gadek, will feature four-cornered fights. One of them is Bukit Katil, where Deputy Defence Minister Adly Zahari, who is Melaka PH chief, is seeking to defend the seat.
Political observers are also keeping a close watch on the four-cornered contest in Bemban, which features candidates from Wawasan and Bersatu, as well as two other contenders. In  2021, Bersatu's Dr Mohd Yadzil Yaakub won the seat on a PN
ticket.
However, following an internal rift within Bersatu that intensified after the expulsion of Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin in February, Yadzil and 16 others were sacked. He later joined Wawasan.
Yadzil is now seeking to defend the seat against Muhammad Rabaie Ab Hamid of Bersatu, Dr Muhammad Solehin Saleh of Bersama and independent candidate Abd Halim Said.
Nearly two-thirds of the 79 candidates, or 49 of them, are aged below 50.
[[nid:1568027]]
The age profile of the candidates comes as parties seek to appeal to a relatively young electorate, with about 65 per cent of the 687,697 eligible voters also below  50.
Despite the multi-cornered contests and slew of hopefuls, Tawfik said the election outcome would also depend on the strategies and approaches adopted by the contesting parties.
"The crucial factors will be grassroots organisation, voter mobilisation and the ability of each candidate to retain support throughout the campaign."
Candidates have until 11.59pm on Nov 13 to canvass for support before polling day on Nov 14.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PN's surrender of Melaka seats to MCA weakens BN leverage in Pas states
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The compromise that settled MCA's seat dispute in Melaka could put Barisan Nasional under pressure to return the favour when electoral negotiations shift to Pas strongholds, analysts say.
International Islamic University Malaysia political analyst Assoc Prof Dr Syaza Shukri said
Perikatan Nasional's surrender of Bandar Hilir and Kota Laksamana to MCA
could raise expectations for BN to make reciprocal concessions in Pas-dominated states.
She said this could shape negotiations in Kedah, Kelantan, Terengganu and Perlis, collectively known as the SG4 states.
"Since PN is giving in to MCA, there might be an expectation that BN would also allow PN to prioritise their parties up north, where there are better chances for PN than BN," she told the New Straits Times.
Syaza said both coalitions needed to project strength in negotiations, with the fluid nature of their relationship explaining why they were maintaining an electoral understanding rather than formalising cooperation.
The adjustment raised MCA's allocation from two to four seats, leaving PN with five of the seven seats initially set aside for the coalition.
Universiti Utara Malaysia political analyst Prof Dr Mohd Azizuddin Mohd Sani said BN's bargaining power in Melaka rested on its position as the incumbent and stronger negotiating partner, allowing it to insist on retaining the 21 seats it previously won.
In Kedah, he said, Pas' dominance could require BN to concede more. Terengganu would present an even sharper test of whether protecting previously won seats was a workable basis for cooperation.
"BN did not give up seats it had won previously in Melaka.
"So would Pas then give no seats in Terengganu, for example, to BN?" he said, adding that wider negotiations could involve trade-offs between BN and Pas strongholds.
Universiti Malaya political analyst Dr Mohammad Tawfik Yaakub said the MCA settlement showed compromise remained possible, but its earlier protest had exposed dissatisfaction over consultation, representation and seat allocation.
He said BN could not expect the Melaka formula to apply in Pas strongholds, especially in seats held by Pas, as cooperation required reciprocal concessions rather than unilateral demands.
"I believe both sides are maintaining an electoral understanding rather than forming a formal coalition because questions over seat distribution, leadership and their component parties' interests remain unresolved," he said.
Such flexibility allowed them to cooperate where their interests converged, Tawfik said, but the 16th General Election would involve much broader and more complicated negotiations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: France protests turn violent as 565 arrested, police injured
Article:
PARIS: Clashes erupted in Paris and other French cities on Saturday after hundreds of thousands of people staged a third weekend of protests at soaring living costs.
More than 500 people were arrested as police fired water cannon and tear gas to disperse rioters on the sidelines of the demonstrations, where regular protesters marched in Halloween costumes.
While Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said the marches had been largely orderly, he denounced the disorder, including an incident in Paris when a police officer was struck by a Molotov cocktail.
The interior ministry said late Saturday that police had arrested 565 people across the country. Four police officers and one gendarme had been injured in Paris, three of them burned by Molotov cocktails.
After a march on the outskirts of Paris in bright sunshine, clashes broke out between police and some demonstrators as the procession reached its final destination.
Dozens of masked people dressed in black used hammers to pry up paving stones and hurl them at police, AFP journalists saw. Police responded with tear gas and several baton charges.
The Paris police prefecture said that several hundred rioters had attacked security forces with projectiles.
Nunez pointed to an "extraordinary" level of violence from some protesters, blaming far-left extremist groups for attacks on security forces.
He described the throwing of a Molotov cocktail at a riot police officer in Paris as an "attempted murder", adding that the officer had escaped with minor injuries.
"We are fully prepared for those looking for confrontation tonight," he warned.
- OFFICER IN FLAMES -
Far-right leader Marine Le Pen said those responsible for the firebomb attack must be "punished with the utmost severity", in a post on X, describing images of the officer in flames as "unbearable."
A night-time curfew was to be imposed in the central Paris neighbourhoods of Republique and Chatelet-Les Halles from 11pm to 6am on Saturday and Sunday.
The interior ministry said that "radical elements" in cities including Bordeaux, Toulouse and Marseille had attempted to enter city centres "with the aim of carrying out vandalism and looting."
In Lyon, France's third-largest city, people threw projectiles at police, prompting officers to fire tear gas.
In the southern city of Toulouse, police used water cannon against an unauthorised protest that drew several thousand people.
- 'ATTACK ON FREEDOM' -
Earlier Saturday, thousands of people, some wearing costumes ranging from Spider-Man to Frankenstein, marched through eastern Paris as a helicopter circled overhead.
Placards read: "No need for tear gas to make our future look bleak" and "Dressed up as an angry citizen for Halloween."
"The fact that demonstrations are being pushed outside city centres, and that so many protests are being banned, is really an attack on freedom," said one demonstrator, Alice Hien, a video game developer.
Authorities said some 320,000 people rallied across France, including 70,000 in Paris.
Youth organisations said nearly half a million people demonstrated, including 200,000 in the capital.
Jean-Luc Melenchon, leader of the far-left France Unbowed party, took part in the Paris march and hailed the strong turnout.
- ELECTIONS LOOMING -
The demonstrations come in a febrile political climate, with presidential elections less than six months away and Le Pen topping opinion polls.
The protest movement, bringing together Yellow Vest activists, trade unions, and high school and university students, initially focused on the rising cost of living, inequality, and deteriorating learning conditions.
Following a security clampdown and serious injuries to some protesters, the movement broadened its demands to include greater protection of civil liberties and the right to protest.
In the northern French city of Lille, 47-year-old Aurelie Herrmann danced at the protest.
"I dance because on television they only show damage and destruction, whereas you can perfectly well demonstrate in good spirits," she said.
Student protesters complained the police had not authorised a march through the centre of the French capital and vowed to stage new blockades of high schools and universities next week, including on Nov 5 when unions have called a demonstration.
With the eurozone's second-largest economy on the brink of recession and under pressure to rein in its debt, the government has limited scope to appease protesters through additional spending.--AFP

Title: Rioters loot shops as Gen Z protests erupt into violence across Germany
Article:
FRANKFURT: Masked rioters looted shops in the German city of Frankfurt on Saturday as massive demonstrations turned violent across the country, with police also firing water cannons at youths hurling Molotov cocktails.
Several police officers were injured in the violence after tens of thousands joined youth-led protests across the country organised by the group "GenZ regelt!" (Gen Z has got this!).
The demonstrations, inspired by similar movements in France and Italy calling for political elites to heed the concerns of the younger generation, were largely peaceful during the day.
But tensions peaked in the evening as some groups of young people refused to disperse, with violence breaking out in major cities including Berlin, Cologne and Hamburg.
It was especially bad in the financial hub of Frankfurt, where police faced protesters hurling stones, fireworks and petrol bombs, and responded with water cannon and pepper spray.
"Violent riots" were taking place, police said in a statement. "Windows have been smashed at several shops. Molotov cocktails are also being thrown at emergency personnel."
A gun store was among the shops looted, with its windows smashed. Police said they arrested a suspect and seized two weapons.
A trainer shop and a perfume store were also targeted, the Bild daily reported.
A large section of Frankfurt's main shopping street was closed off as authorities sought to quell the unrest, with police vans and riot police stopping anyone from entering, according to an AFP journalist.
A police helicopter hovered overhead as sporadic blasts were heard on the street.
At least one police officer was injured there and was receiving medical treatment.
- 'SHAMEFUL' -
Roman Poseck, interior minister of Hesse state, said that "around 100 clearly identified left-wing extremists" had infiltrated the protest in Frankfurt.
"It is shameful how this event here in Frankfurt has ended."
Police also used water cannon in the cities of Hamburg and Cologne after they said demonstrators targeted emergency service workers with fireworks, stones and bottles.
In Berlin, a protest not organised by the "GenZ regelt!" movement took place in the evening, with police reporting they were pelted with eggs and bottles.
A police officer in Bonn suffered minor injuries during a confrontation with a group.
Police were reported to have arrested large numbers of rioters.
The youth-led protests earlier in the day took place in a mostly peaceful and festive atmosphere.
Some people were dressed in outfits ranging from dinosaurs to Batman as the demonstrations coincided with Halloween.
They waved signs that read "Time for resistance", and "Merz must go", in reference to conservative Chancellor Friedrich Merz.
"I think it's really important to show solidarity with all the other protests currently happening across Europe, including in France," Milla, a 20-year-old student who only gave her first name, told AFP in Berlin.
"I've been waiting for a long time for something to finally really happen, and for people to tackle this with a bit more force. I believe that today here is the first step."
The movement's complaints range from the high cost of living to poorly maintained schools and government spending cuts.
More broadly it objects to what it sees as politicians making decisions with apparently little regard for the younger generation.
They are also unhappy with sharply increased military spending and a new voluntary service model aimed at boosting troop numbers, fearing it is a step towards bringing back conscription.
- EUROPE-WIDE PROTESTS -
"GenZ regelt!" said some 120,000 people took part in the demonstrations, below around 180,000 they had been expecting.
Protests also took place in France Saturday for a third straight weekend, with clashes erupting in Paris and elsewhere.
Nationwide demonstrations there on Oct 17 degenerated into some of the country's worst rioting in years.
Berlin has been in contact with officials in France and Italy amid fears that radicals from overseas could seek to join the German protests.
The "GenZ regelt!" movement explicitly rejected violence.
"Extremist groups, anti-constitutional symbols, racism and hate speech have no place with us – no matter from which side," it said.--AFP
