Title: King Charles to address Commonwealth with 'unflinching honesty' amid slavery focus
Article:
ST. JOHN'S, Antigua and Barbuda: King Charles III will confront "shameful aspects" of UK history with "unflinching honesty" when he addresses Commonwealth leaders next week, Buckingham Palace said Saturday, amid renewed scrutiny of Britain's role in historical transatlantic slavery.
The comments come after Prime Minister Andy Burnham revealed he was open to the UK formally apologising for its role in the trade, but ruling out paying the financial reparations demanded by some Caribbean countries.
The issues have resurfaced as Charles tours the Caribbean before delivering a speech Tuesday at the Commonwealth heads of government meeting there, which Burnham is also set to attend.
"The King will not shy away from confronting the most shameful aspects of the past during this visit," a palace spokesperson said.
"You may therefore expect him to address them in his speech with unflinching honesty, sincere sorrow, and respect for the wider discussions that will be taking place between relevant governments on this issue."
The palace noted the monarch, who arrived in Antigua and Barbuda late Friday ahead of the summit there, will be speaking in his role as head of the 56-member Commonwealth, composed mainly of former British colonies.
"It would not be appropriate for him to address matters of particular policy relating to the UK government's position," the spokesperson said.
They added that the king will "primarily focus on encouraging practical solutions and united efforts to address global challenges and opportunities."
- SLAVERY PRESSURE -
Under pressure from Commonwealth countries over Britain's pivotal part in transatlantic slavery, Burnham penned a newspaper op-ed published earlier Saturday that argued: "We need to face up to the past."
Writing in The Guardian, he pledged to have "difficult conversations" to safeguard the Commonwealth's future, offering a "structured dialogue with those affected."
"Listening to calls for a formal apology on behalf of the British state will form an important part of this process and I am open to them," Burnham wrote.
Expressing "sorrow and regret for the pain and suffering of so many millions" resulting from the trade and its links to the present day, he insisted reparations were not "the right answer."
"I do not think that British people today can be held liable for historical wrongs, however heinous, that happened in a different age under different laws and in which they played no personal part," he wrote.
The centre-left British leader also announced he would launch a new debt restructuring drive for the poorest Commonwealth countries, led by former Labour prime minister Gordon Brown.
He vowed to work with "global partners" to help those countries repay "over a longer time period and with better rates."
- REPARATION CALLS -
The issues have loomed large over 77-year-old Charles's ongoing nine-day visit to three Caribbean countries.
"I do believe there should be an apology," receptionist Daliesha Murray told AFP as the king arrived Tuesday in The Bahamas, where small groups of protesters waved placards reading: "Pay what you owe us."
The monarch acknowledged "the great suffering of the past" during that stop.
In Guyana on Friday, he visited a site of execution of local people during British colonial rule, pausing to reflect in a gesture seen as indicating his awareness of that past injustice.
Ahead of a meeting with Charles during that leg, Guyana's President Irfaan Ali told ITV News that recognising historical wrongs was just a "first step."
"Now, moving to the apology is the next step," he said.
Britain has never formally apologised for slavery or agreed to pay reparations.
The country profited for centuries from colonialism and slavery, but argues it also led the way in the latter's abolition.
In 1833, the UK parliament passed a law to abolish slavery in most of the British Empire.
In a sign of the domestic political opposition Burnham could face in issuing a formal apology, Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said Saturday there was "no need" while reiterating her opposition to reparations.
She urged the Commonwealth to "look forward" and "not endlessly backwards."
"Slavery was an evil in which people from every continent and region participated," she wrote on X.
"We should be honest about the whole history, not select the parts that are politically convenient today."--AFP

Title: Tok Mat to lead Malaysia’s delegation to CHOGM 2026 in Antigua and Barbuda
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 1 — Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan will lead Malaysia’s delegation to the 28th Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM 2026) and related meetings in St. John’s, Antigua and Barbuda, from November 1 to 4.
In a statement, the Foreign Ministry, also known as Wisma Putra, said CHOGM 2026, themed “Accelerating Partnerships and Investment for a Prosperous Commonwealth”, will bring together Heads of State/Government and Ministers from 56 Commonwealth Member States.
“The Foreign Minister will participate in a series of high-level meetings and hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts. Discussions will focus on strengthening South-South Cooperation, narrowing the global development gap and fostering trade and investment among Commonwealth countries,” the statement read.
Wisma Putra said Malaysia’s participation in CHOGM 2026 reaffirms the Government’s commitment to promoting the principles and values enshrined in the Commonwealth Charter and strengthening cooperation among Member States. — Bernama

Title: DBKL urges responsible lift use after viral clip shows motorcycle inside PPR elevator (VIDEO)
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 1 — City Hall (DBKL) has urged residents and delivery riders to treat public housing amenities with care, following a viral video showing an individual riding a motorcycle into a People’s Housing Project (PPR) lift.
The closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage, which circulated widely across social media, sparked public outrage over safety hazards and property damage. Neither the identity of the rider nor the precise location of the building has been independently verified.
In a statement, DBKL did not call out the individual but addressed the broader habit of rolling motorcycles and electric scooters into residential elevators to expedite doorstep deliveries.
“DBKL understands the demands of a food delivery rider’s job and appreciates their role in making city life easier.
“But the convenience of earning a living should go hand in hand with the responsibility to respect the rules and look after shared facilities,” DBKL said.
City Hall stressed that functioning elevators are an essential lifeline for public housing (PA) and PPR residents, especially senior citizens, persons with disabilities (OKU), expectant mothers, and young families. It added that ongoing maintenance, repairs, and refurbishment works are carried out regularly to ensure passenger safety.
The authority noted that frequent breakdowns drain municipal resources and severely disrupt residents’ daily routines.
“Some damage can actually be avoided if every user is more responsible,” the statement said, questioning whether residents who frequently lament broken lifts consider the toll of careless usage.
DBKL reiterated that earning a living must not compromise civic regulations or communal infrastructure.
“DBKL can provide, maintain and improve facilities, but cooperation and concern from all parties are needed to keep them working in the long term,” it said, adding that safeguarding public amenities reflects the civic responsibility expected of urban dwellers.

Title: New Chinese ambassador Yao Wen outlines four key priorities to deepen Malaysia-China ties
Article:
SEPANG, Nov 1 — Newly appointed Chinese Ambassador to Malaysia Yao Wen has pledged to further strengthen bilateral relations, with greater emphasis on economic cooperation, emerging technologies and people-to-people exchanges.
In his written address upon arriving at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) yesterday, Yao said his key priorities included translating the consensus reached by leaders of both countries into concrete actions and advancing cooperation in areas such as infrastructure, trade, artificial intelligence (AI) and semiconductors.
“It is a great pleasure to be back in Malaysia, a beautiful country known as ‘Malaysia, Truly Asia’, as I step into my new role. After years working in the region and visiting Malaysia numerous times, I have always held a special place for this country in my heart.
“My ultimate goal is to advance all-dimensional cooperation and friendly exchanges, fostering an even closer bond between our two peoples. To this end, I look forward to working hand in hand with our Malaysian friends to pursue four key priorities,” he said.
Yao, 53, arrived from Beijing on Saturday night via an Air China flight, succeeding Ouyang Yujing as China’s ambassador to Malaysia. He was received by representatives from the Foreign Ministry’s Protocol and Consular Department.
As the first priority, Yao said both countries should strengthen political mutual trust and consolidate their longstanding friendship.
He said China was advancing its national rejuvenation through Chinese modernisation, while Malaysia was making strategic progress under the Malaysia Madani vision.
He said the two countries were well positioned to support each other’s modernisation efforts, deepen strategic mutual trust and ensure the steady, long-term development of their high-level strategic community with a shared future.
As the first priority, Yao said both countries should strengthen political mutual trust and consolidate their longstanding friendship. — Bernama pic
On economic cooperation, Yao said both countries should advance the high-quality development of the Belt and Road Initiative, strengthening cooperation in traditional sectors such as infrastructure and trade while exploring new opportunities in AI and semiconductors.
On the third priority, he called for deeper people-to-people exchanges, describing close ties between the peoples of both countries as the foundation of sound bilateral relations.
“Both countries should leverage their mutual visa-free policy and the opportunity presented by Visit Malaysia Year 2026 to strengthen cooperation in education, culture, healthcare, tourism and exchanges at the sub-national level,” he added.
He also expressed hope for the successful hosting of the Confucian-Islamic Civilisational Dialogues to further promote mutual understanding and bring the peoples of both countries closer.
On the fourth priority, Yao called for stronger multilateral coordination between Malaysia and China to promote international fairness and justice.
“Together, China and Malaysia must uphold the international system with the United Nations at its core, champion international fairness and justice, and amplify the voice of the Global South to forge a more equitable global governance system.
“By staying committed to openness and development, and pioneering rules for emerging domains, we can inject much-needed certainty into a world fraught with turbulence and volatility,” he said.
Yao said he was committed to building on the legacy of his predecessors and working closely with Malaysians from all walks of life to deepen comprehensive cooperation and strengthen the longstanding friendship between the two countries.
He said both sides should continue fostering dialogue, sharing insights and pooling their wisdom to strengthen bilateral ties and bring enduring prosperity to their peoples for generations to come. — Bernama

Title: Former AG Idrus Harun among four appointed as members of Judicial Appointments Commission
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 1 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has appointed four individuals, including former Attorney General Tan Sri Idrus Harun, as members of the Judicial Appointments Commission for a two-year term, effective today.
Also appointed are former Federal Court Judge Tan Sri Zainun Ali; Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) law lecturer Prof. Dr. Hartini Saripan (for a second term); and former Sabah State Attorney General Datuk Mariati Robert.
The Office of the Secretary of the Judicial Appointments Commission, in a statement today, said the appointments were made in accordance with subsection 5(1)(f) of the Judicial Appointments Commission Act 2009 [Act 695].
“These appointments are for a two-year term, effective from November 1, 2026, to October 31, 2028,” the statement read.
The Judicial Appointments Commission also expressed its appreciation and gratitude to Datuk Seri Talat Mahmood Abdul Rashid for his service and contributions during his tenure as a member of the Commission. — Bernama

Title: PM: RM2.5m to provide dialysis facilities at selected Kelantan mosques, plus RM645,000 for water, solar projects
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Nov 1 — The government has allocated RM2.5 million to provide dialysis facilities at selected mosques in Kelantan in collaboration with Yayasan Waqaf Malaysia (YWM) and Radicare.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the initiative would improve access to treatment, particularly for rural kidney patients who have to travel long distances to receive dialysis.
He said using mosques as dialysis centres would also expand their role in serving local communities.
“We are working with Radicare to make dialysis facilities more accessible, particularly for villagers who have to travel far for treatment. We are using mosques as the base for these facilities,” he said at the Sebarkan Salam@Kota Bharu Berselawat programme at the grounds of Masjid Muhammadi here last night.
Also present were Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan, his deputy Marhamah Rosli and Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud.
Anwar said another RM645,000 had been allocated through YWM for water waqf projects and solar installations at selected mosques in Kelantan facing shortages of basic amenities.
He also announced a special allocation of RM500,000 for maintenance and upgrading works, including hostel facilities, at Sekolah Menengah Ugama Darul Ulum Al-Muhammadiyyah in Padang Kolam here. — Bernama

Title: Avoid 3R provocations, campaign fairly, maturely and with dignity, Azalina tells Melaka poll candidates
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 1 — All candidates, party campaign machinery and supporters of parties contesting the 16th Melaka State Election have been urged to campaign in a fair, mature and dignified manner throughout the 14-day campaign period.
Umno Information Chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said also reminded them to comply with election laws and regulations set by the Election Commission (EC), respect differing views and avoid provocations involving sensitivities related to religion, race and the royal institution (3R).
“Elections should provide an opportunity for candidates to present and debate their ideas, policies and public service commitments, not create hostility or deepen divisions among the people,” she said in a statement yesterday.
Azalina stressed Barisan Nasional’s (BN) position that election campaigns should be centred on candidates’ credentials, service records, manifestos and policy proposals to help voters evaluate their capabilities, experience and vision for Melaka’s future.
She said BN would not engage in smear campaigns or black PR, as the coalition wanted to secure a mandate based on its own strengths rather than by undermining others, emphasising that the people of Melaka had the right to make their choices based on facts, not slander or hatred.
Azalina, also the Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform), reminded the public to be more vigilant about the challenges posed by the digital environment and make it a habit to verify sources, check facts and think before sharing information.
She urged the public to report content suspected of containing false news, defamatory material, impersonation or 3R-related violations through the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission’s official channels, while election offences should be reported to the EC, police or the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission.
“For content taken down by digital platforms, users can make use of the appeals channels provided by the respective platforms. They should also keep all relevant evidence, including screenshots, links and timestamps, to ensure that any complaints can be properly reviewed,” she said.
Meanwhile, she said Umno’s information machinery at all levels should place greater emphasis on strengthening its digital communications campaign, as social media has become one of the main channels through which voters obtain information and form their views in yesterday’s political landscape.
According to Azalina, the fact that 43.6 per cent of Melaka’s electorate comprises voters aged between 21 and 40 underscores the need for Umno to adopt a more dynamic, creative and youth-oriented communications approach.
“Make sure the digital space is filled with accurate information, engaging content and explanations that are factual and conveyed responsibly,” she said.
Azalina also called on voters to assess each candidate and the proposals put forward rationally and maturely, based on facts, and to fulfil their responsibility on polling day.
Early voting for the 16th Melaka state polls is scheduled for Nov 10, while polling day is set for Nov 14.
For the latest updates on the 16th Melaka State Election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/ — Bernama

Title: Melaka deserves trustworthy, hardworking leaders with integrity, says Anwar
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 1 — Melaka deserves trustworthy, hardworking leaders with integrity who are committed to the well-being of its people, said Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
The Prime Minister expressed confidence that voters in the 16th Melaka state election would choose PH candidates who are committed to bringing meaningful improvements and positive change to the people of the state.
“Melaka deserves leaders who are trustworthy, have integrity and are dedicated to working for the people and their well-being.
“I am confident that the people of Melaka will choose HARAPAN candidates who will work to bring meaningful improvements and real change to the state. Melaka Rumah Kita! (Melaka Our Home),” he said in a Facebook post today.
PH is contesting 24 of the 28 seats in the state election, fielding 10 candidates from PKR and seven each from DAP and Parti Amanah Negara.
The Election Commission has set Nov 14 as polling day, with early voting scheduled for Nov 10.
For the latest news on the 16th Melaka state election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/. — Bernama

Title: Anwar prays for Sultan Sharafuddin’s speedy recovery from Influenza A
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 1 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has prayed for the recovery of the Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, who is unwell after contracting Influenza A.
He also prayed that His Royal Highness would always be under the protection and blessings of Allah SWT.
“May Allah SWT grant His Royal Highness Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah Alhaj Ibni Almarhum Sultan Salahuddin Abdul Aziz Shah Alhaj, Sultan and Ruler of Selangor Darul Ehsan, a speedy recovery and good health,” he said in a Facebook post yesterday.
Earlier, Istana Alam Shah said in a statement that the infection had been detected by the Sultan’s two personal physicians, Datuk Dr Anuar Onah and Datuk Dr Tan Hui Meng, after Sultan Sharafuddin had been experiencing a high fever and weakness in his limbs since the previous morning.
Following this, Sultan Sharafuddin was advised to rest and refrain from attending any functions for five to seven days to allow him to recover fully. — Bernama

Title: Driver blames Waze after tour bus wedges under bridge with 30 aboard in Butterworth
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 1 — A tour bus carrying over 30 passengers from Johor became wedged under a flyover in Taman Bagan of Butterworth, Penang, last night after the driver alleged followed directions from the Waze navigation app.
The crash lodged nearly half the bus beneath the low-clearance structure, shattering several windows and showering the road with glass shards. Two passengers suffered minor injuries from flying glass but are reported to be in stable condition,
Berita Harian
reported.
The driver said he was ferrying the tour group to a nearby hotel before continuing their journey to Kedah today.
He explained that he relied on Waze, which routed him along the road without factoring in the height limit of the overhead bridge.
“I heard a loud crashing sound while driving underneath the flyover. A few seconds later, the bus windows shattered and glass fragments were scattered everywhere.
“I was very shocked by what happened,” he said.
Razali said that while he had visited Butterworth several times previously, this was the first time he had used Waze to navigate through Taman Bagan. Poor lighting and his unfamiliarity with the neighbourhood prompted him to rely entirely on the app’s directions, he said.
A check at the site revealed a 2.6-metre height clearance sign posted before the flyover, alongside a warning sign alerting motorists to frequent collisions in the area.

Title: Anwar: Islamic education in Kelantan gets continued support with RM9.36m for 23 schools, plus RM6.6m more
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Nov 1 — The government will continue to strengthen the development of Islamic education in Kelantan through continuous financial assistance, infrastructure upgrades and the empowerment of traditional educational institutions, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said this commitment is being translated into action through various targeted initiatives to ensure that Islamic educational institutions in the state, particularly religious and pondok schools (traditional Islamic religious schools), operate in a conducive learning environment.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said the government allocated RM9.36 million to 23 Islamic educational institutions in Kelantan in 2025, and approved an additional RM6.628 million this year to support 42 other institutions.
“I know my responsibility... while I have the opportunity and authority, I want to do the best I can so that people will perceive this administration, led by Muslims, as fair and wise, and does its best to elevate the dignity of the people and the nation,” he said in his speech at the ‘Sebarkan Salam@Kota Bharu Berselawat’ Programme held at the grounds of Masjid Muhammadi here last night.
Also present were the Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs), Dr Zulkifli Hasan, and his deputy, Marhamah Rosli, as well as Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud.
Anwar said the government had also set aside funds for periodic maintenance and repair works, as well as initiatives to upgrade mosque facilities and provide dialysis treatment support for those in need.
He also announced the approval for the use of robotic surgical technology at Hospital Universiti Sains Malaysia (HUSM) in Kubang Kerian to enhance the quality of healthcare services in the state for the comfort of patients. — Bernama

Title: Govt committed to opening university pathways for ‘pondok’ students, says PM
Article:
PASIR MAS, Nov 1 — The government is committed to creating opportunities for students of pondok (traditional Islamic religious schools) to pursue higher education up to university level, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said the move was important to ensure that pondok institutions were not marginalised but instead recognised and strengthened, enabling their students to keep pace with national development without compromising their Islamic scholarly foundations.
Several Islamic scholars had been tasked with formulating proposals to make it happen, he said after performing Maghrib prayers at Madrasah Ar-Rahmaniah Ad-Diniah Pondok Lubuk Tapah here yesterday. Also present was Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud.
Meanwhile, Anwar said pondok institutions served a role beyond religious education, acting as a bastion for safeguarding Islamic faith and strengthening the Muslim community.
He said these institutions also played an important role in preserving religious values, identity and national harmony.
He added that the government would continue to improve the education system and upgrade pondok facilities nationwide to provide a more conducive learning environment for students.
Earlier, Anwar also presented a RM200,000 contribution to Madrasah Ar-Rahmaniah Ad-Diniah Pondok Lubuk Tapah. — Bernama

Title: Palace: Selangor Sultan contracts Influenza A, investiture ceremony postponed
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 1 — The Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, has contracted Influenza A and has been advised to rest for five to seven days to ensure a full recovery.
Istana Alam Shah said in a statement yesterday that His Royal Highness’s personal physicians, Datuk Dr Anuar Onah and Datuk Dr Tan Hui Meng, detected symptoms of the infection on Friday morning after the Sultan developed a high fever and body weakness.
The statement said the Selangor ruler was believed to have contracted the virus while attending public functions and interacting with members of the public, including at outdoor events.
“His Royal Highness’s health is gradually improving, although he still has a fever. The attending doctors have advised him to rest and refrain from attending any functions for five to seven days to allow for a full recovery,” it said.
Following the development, the investiture ceremony for Selangor state honours, scheduled for tomorrow (November 1) in conjunction with the Silver Jubilee celebration of the Sultan’s reign, has been postponed to November 7.
Istana Alam Shah urged all parties involved to take note of the revised date and thanked them for their cooperation and understanding.
It also called on the public to pray for the Sultan’s speedy recovery and continued good health. — Bernama

Title: Mother, daughter arrested after stray dog operation scuffle injures Muar council officer
Article:
MUAR, Nov 1 — Police have arrested a mother and daughter for allegedly obstructing and injuring a female Muar Municipal Council (MPM) enforcement officer during dog-catching operation in Bukit Pasir.
The incident occurred at Taman Bintang Emas around 5.55am on Thursday, later triggering public outcry after photos of the injured officer lying on the pavement circulated widely on social media.
Muar district police chief Assistant Commissioner Raiz Mukhliz Azman Aziz said the suspects, aged 52 and 24, were detained to facilitate investigations into obstructing a public servant from discharging their duties.
“During the operation, the two women had allegedly challenged the actions of the enforcement officers and obstructed them from carrying out their duties by attempting to release the captured dogs.
“A struggle ensued before a female enforcement officer fell when she attempted to defuse the tense situation,” he said in a statement last night.
A medical examination confirmed that the 45-year-old enforcement officer sustained bruising to both arms. She subsequently lodged a police report over the altercation.
“Following the police report, the mother and daughter were later arrested at their residence in Bukit Pasir yesterday to assist with investigations,” he said.
Urine screenings conducted on both women returned negative for illicit substances.
The Magistrate’s Court here has granted investigators a two-day remand order against both suspects.
The case is being investigated under Section 186 of the Penal Code for obstructing a public servant in the discharge of public functions, alongside Section 353 for using criminal force to deter a public servant from performing their duty. Both offences carry a maximum penalty of two years’ imprisonment, a fine, or both upon conviction.
Raiz Mukhliz noted that officers are actively recording witness statements and compiling evidence.
“We advise the public to cooperate during any enforcement operations and refrain from any actions that could obstruct public servants from carrying out their duties,” he said.

Title: Kerian flood evacuees fall to 18 as situation improves
Article:
IPOH, Nov 1 — The number of flood victims in the Kerian district has decreased, with 18 individuals from seven families remaining at a relief centre (PPS), down from 25 individuals from nine families yesterday.
The Secretariat of the Perak State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN) said that as of 8am today, all the victims are still sheltering at the PPS at Sekolah Kebangsaan Titi Serong.
The victims, all from Taman Aman Sejahtera and Taman Desa Aman 1, have been housed at the centre since last Thursday.
Meanwhile, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has forecast thunderstorms this afternoon across all districts, except Kerian, Manjung, and Bagan Datuk. — Bernama

Title: Flushed, binned, forgotten: How unwanted medicines are putting Malaysia’s waterways at risk (VIDEO)
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 1 — From
disrupting fish reproduction
to altering aquatic behaviour, pharmaceutical residues can have far-reaching effects on ecosystems when expired or unwanted medicines are improperly discarded.
Yet for many households, disposing of old medicines remains an afterthought, with the rubbish bin often the most convenient option when returning them to a healthcare facility or pharmacy seems too troublesome.
As pharmaceutical consumption rises alongside Malaysia’s growing and ageing population, the volume of unwanted medicines requiring proper disposal is also likely to increase.
According to the Health Ministry’s Pharmaceutical Services Programme (PSP), many people mistakenly believe expired medicines can be thrown away with household waste, while others bury unused medication under the assumption that it is safer.
“All pharmaceutical products, including traditional preparations and supplements, must not be disposed of with household waste or flushed down toilets or sinks.
“This includes tablets, capsules, pills, liquid medications, inhalers, topical preparations (ointments and creams), eye and nasal drops, suppositories, sachets and patches.
“Active pharmaceutical ingredients and excipients in improperly discarded medicines can contaminate drinking water sources and aquatic ecosystems, entering drainage systems through landfill leachate or wastewater when medicines are flushed down sinks or toilets,” it said in response to recent queries from
Malay Mail
.
The PSP also sought to dispel the misconception that medicines returned to healthcare facilities would be reused for other patients, stressing that they must instead be disposed of safely in line with international recommendations.
It warned that improper disposal of antibiotics could also contribute to antimicrobial resistance, potentially making commonly used antibiotics less effective against infections and posing serious challenges to healthcare systems.
Studies worldwide have detected pharmaceutical residues in waterways, with improper medicine disposal among the contributing factors. — Picture by Choo Choy May
What gets thrown away
In Malaysia, the Health Ministry’s
MyMediSAFE
programme, launched in September 2024, leads efforts to educate the public on the safe disposal of unused and expired medicines through strategic partnerships with the private sector.
According to the 2025 edition of MyMediSAFE’s Master Plan for the Disposal of Medicines Kept by Patients for Environmental Sustainability, a 2019 study involving 426 respondents in Selangor found that 84.9 per cent disposed of unused medicines in household rubbish bins, while only 15.1 per cent were aware of proper disposal methods.
Another study in 2021 found that about two-thirds of 1,000 patients with chronic conditions surveyed in the Klang Valley disposed of unused medicines with household waste, poured them down drains or flushed them down toilets.
A separate
study
examining 1,052 rivers across 104 countries ranked Selangor’s Sungai Langat among the 20 most polluted by pharmaceutical residues, detecting carbamazepine, an anticonvulsant, and metformin, a diabetes medication, in water samples.
There are currently 1,248 medicine collection points nationwide, including Health Ministry hospitals, selected private and university hospitals, and community pharmacies participating in MyMediSAFE.
The scale of the problem is also reflected in figures from the Malaysian Pharmacists Society (MPS), which collected an estimated 639kg of unused and expired medicines between January and June this year through a nationwide programme supporting independent community pharmacies as medicine-return points.
Despite these efforts, awareness of proper medicine disposal remains a challenge.
Malaysian Pharmacists Society’s safe medicine disposal special interest group chairman Ng Yi Ling says tackling medicine wastage starts with understanding why patients accumulate unused medication at home. — Picture by Choo Choy May
Ng Yi Ling, chairman of the MPS Special Interest Group on safe medicine disposal, said unused and expired medicines often accumulate at home because people are unaware of existing disposal services or do not regularly check their medicine supplies.
“Many people may not be aware of the consequences of improper medicine disposal; even among those who are aware, they may not consider its importance so it stops there.
“I think another reason, especially among patients on chronic medication, is confusion over dosage. For instance, a patient prescribed four metformin tablets a day may take only two, either out of fear of side effects or a lack of understanding, eventually accumulating excess medication at home,” she told
Malay Mail
.
Beyond the environmental risks, Ng said medicines discarded in rubbish bins could cause accidental poisoning if children or animals mistook them for food and ingested them.
She also highlighted the financial cost of medicine wastage, noting that pharmaceutical production requires significant resources, while patients who fail to take medication as prescribed risk worsening their conditions, potentially requiring further treatment and increasing healthcare costs.
Tackling the waste
Ng, who is also Alpro Pharmacy’s professional care and development manager, said preventing improper disposal should begin with understanding why patients accumulate unused medication.
Pharmacists, she said, have a key role in identifying patients’ concerns and encouraging them to take their medicines as prescribed.
She cited cases of patients accumulating excess medication after failing to follow their prescribed treatment, including one who stopped taking diabetes medication in favour of alternative treatments.
“Pharmacists should not simply accept returned medicines and dispose of them but ask patients why they have excess medication.
“By addressing concerns such as fear of side effects or confusion over dosage, we can prevent medicine wastage at its source and ensure unused medicines are disposed of safely,” she said.
Unwanted medicines can be returned to designated collection points, including participating pharmacies, under the Health Ministry’s MyMediSAFE programme, which currently has 1,248 locations nationwide. — Picture by Choo Choy May
Alpro has disposed of an average of 3.5 tonnes of unused medicines returned by the public each year over the past three years.
However, Ng said the volume was hardly cause for celebration, as it also reflected patients not taking their medication as prescribed.
Among the most commonly returned medicines were metformin for diabetes and statins for high cholesterol, both prescribed for chronic conditions, alongside painkillers such as paracetamol and smaller quantities of antibiotics.
Ng said educational efforts were also being introduced in schools, with animations used to teach children about the risks of improper medicine disposal and the importance of safe disposal practices.
“Now that the resources and disposal services are in place, we hope to engage the wider community through outreach programmes and encourage them to work together with the Health Ministry and MPS, which have been driving these efforts,” she said.
With more medicine collection points available nationwide under MyMediSAFE, the PSP encouraged Malaysians to make safe disposal a regular habit.
“They no longer need to make special trips to specific healthcare facilities, as more collection points are now available for them to visit while going about their other activities.
“The public is encouraged to use medicines responsibly by finishing existing supplies at home before obtaining more and informing pharmacy staff of any remaining medication so they can assess patients’ needs and dispense only the quantities required,” it said.

Title: Fahmi offers condolences to family of Mata Ayer state assemblyman Wan Badariah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil has expressed his condolences to the family of Mata Ayer State Assemblyman Wan Badariah Wan Saad, who passed away today.
“My deepest condolences to the entire family of the deceased, as well as to her friends and fellow comrades,” he said in a Facebook post.
Fahmi also prayed that Allah SWT would forgive the deceased’s sins, bless her soul, and place her among the believers and the righteous.
Wan Badariah passed away at Tuanku Fauziah Hospital in Kangar at 4.26pm.
The deceased won the Mata Ayer seat under the Perikatan Nasional ticket during the 15th General Election with a majority of 2,021 votes. — Bernama

Title: Anwar directs Education Ministry to act firmly on school bullying
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Oct 31 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has directed the Ministry of Education (MOE) to take firm action against bullying in schools amid growing concerns over children’s safety and well-being.
He said cases involving children, including suicide, abuse and bullying, highlighted the need to strengthen character development and moral values from an early age.
Anwar said academic excellence alone was insufficient, stressing that education must also instil good manners, respect and a sense of responsibility among students.
“Bullying and humiliating others show that there are still shortcomings in instilling values and proper conduct in our education system.
“The Education Ministry has been directed to be firm and take decisive action. Teachers and educators must also help look after our children,” he said at the launch of the Kelantan Entrepreneur Revival Scheme here today.
Anwar also stressed the importance of religious education, including understanding and practising the teachings of the Quran, performing prayers and respecting parents, teachers and peers.
He said addressing social problems such as drug abuse and crime required a comprehensive approach to ensure young people grew up in a healthy environment. — Bernama

Title: Anwar, Lawrence Wong to witness JS-SEZ master plan launch; Perak venue under review, says Akmal Nasrullah
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 31 — The government is considering Perak as the venue for the launch of the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) master plan, which could coincide with the two countries’ Annual Leaders’ Retreat scheduled to be held in the state on December 4.
Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said it had been agreed that the launch would be witnessed jointly by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his Singaporean counterpart, Lawrence Wong.
“Both prime ministers have agreed to witness the launch of the master plan. We are now finalising the venue, as this year’s Annual Leaders’ Retreat is expected to be held in Ipoh.
“We are considering whether the launch will take place there or whether other arrangements will be made. However, both prime ministers have agreed to witness the ceremony,” he told a press conference after the Johor Bahru parliamentary constituency’s Deepavali celebration in Larkin here today.
On preparations for Monday’s bilateral meeting in Singapore, Akmal Nasrullah said Singapore would host the meeting.
He described the meeting as significant as it would be the first to be held under the Johor-Singapore Cooperation Ministerial Committee framework.
He is scheduled to lead the Malaysian delegation alongside Johor Menteri Besar Onn Hafiz Ghazi, while Singapore’s delegation will be led by National Development Minister Chee Hong Tat.
“From Malaysia’s perspective, this meeting presents an opportunity to assess progress in implementing the JS-SEZ initiative and discuss plans for the way forward,” he said.
Akmal Nasrullah said the programme framework and logistical arrangements for the Annual Leaders’ Retreat were being refined to maximise its impact following the launch of the master plan.
On the Deepavali celebration, he said a total of RM318,000 had been allocated to improve community well-being in the Johor Bahru parliamentary constituency.
He presented RM260,000 under the Prime Minister’s Office’s Madani Infrastructure and Social Response Programme (PRISMA) for repairs to staircase handrails at Rumah Pangsa Serantau Baru in Larkin.
He said the infrastructure improvements were aimed at enhancing residents’ safety and comfort, particularly for senior citizens, children and other vulnerable groups.
A further RM47,500 was allocated to upgrade places of worship serving the Indian community, while RM10,500 was distributed among four local non-governmental organisations to support welfare, cultural and community development programmes. — Bernama

Title: National Courier Day: Govt pledges reform as RM6.9b courier sector takes spotlight
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 31 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil today launched the National Courier Day 2026 (HKN2026) celebration, recognising the industry’s RM6.9 billion contribution to the country’s digital economy, at the Selangor International Trade Centre.
Themed “Sustaining the Industry, Strengthening Trust,” the event was organised by the Malaysian Express Carriers Association (AMEC) with support from the Communications Ministry through the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC).
MCMC said the government remains committed to strengthening the postal and courier industry through regulatory reform, strategic cooperation and digital transformation to improve service efficiency, industry competitiveness and consumer safety.
“On regulatory reform, the government is reviewing proposed amendments to the Postal Services Act 2012 (Act 741) and plans to gazette the Postal Services Regulations (Postal Service Security and Prohibited Postal Articles) 2026 (PSR2026), subject to the relevant approval process.
“These measures aim to strengthen security, industry accountability and consumer protection, in step with the rapid growth of e-commerce,” MCMC said in a statement today.
Also present were Communications Ministry secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah, MCMC managing director Abdul Karim Fakir Ali, AMEC chairman Ronald Tan, and representatives of government agencies, postal and courier industry players.
Parcel Shield, an initiative led by the Postal Forum with MCMC support, was also launched at HKN2026 to tackle parcel delivery fraud.
“The initiative, among others, encourages information sharing between courier companies and e-commerce platforms, and the dissemination of fraud alerts to enhance consumer protection and confidence,” the statement read.
HKN2026 further saw the signing of a memorandum of collaboration for the Courier Network Sharing initiative, a last-mile delivery pilot at selected locations.
“The project will assess the potential for infrastructure optimisation, reduced operational overlap and improved service access before expansion is considered,” the statement read.
Additionally, digital transformation is being strengthened through the National Address System (NAS) to improve address accuracy and delivery efficiency, and PAKEJ Map, which helps users locate more than 47,000 postal and courier service points nationwide.
HKN2026 further recognised industry personnel through the Best Courier Worker award, the Safe Driving Challenge and the MyCSP Courier Safety Passport programme, with emphasis on safety and service quality. — Bernama

Title: Nga Kor Ming urges global cooperation on housing crisis, cites 3.4 billion affected
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — Stronger international cooperation is needed to address the global housing crisis, with approximately 3.4 billion people worldwide experiencing some form of inadequate housing, said Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming.
In making the call, Nga, who is also United Nations Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat) Assembly president, said that more than 1.16 billion people lived in informal settlements, including slums, while 44 per cent of urban renters spent an unsustainable proportion of their income on rent.
“Governments must ensure that housing is affordable, safe, well-connected to public transport and employment opportunities, and supported by essential public amenities,” he said in his keynote address at the opening ceremony of the Global Observance of World Cities Day 2026 in Fuzhou, China, today.
The event, themed “Regenerating the City: Adequate Housing for All”, is jointly organised by UN-Habitat, China’s Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development, the Fujian Provincial People’s Government and the Fuzhou Municipal People’s Government.
Nga said addressing the crisis required more than building additional homes, as rising housing costs placed increasing pressure on households and widened social inequalities.
He urged governments, international organisations, and the private sector to strengthen partnerships in affordable housing, green development and sustainable urban regeneration.
Sharing Malaysia’s experience, Nga said the government had set a target of delivering one million affordable homes between 2026 and 2035, alongside an ambition to place Malaysia among the world’s top 10 countries for home ownership by 2035.
He highlighted the Malaysia Madani vision, the country’s housing reform agenda, and the National Housing Policy 2026-2035 as key initiatives to improve housing accessibility and support sustainable urban development.
Nga also cited the RM60 billion Housing Credit Guarantee Scheme (SJKP), which facilitates access to home financing for 150,000 individuals without conventional income documentation.
“Housing is the foundational soil from which all human capability grows. It is where our children form their earliest ambitions, where working parents recharge their spirit, and where our senior citizens enjoy the honour they have earned over a lifetime.
“When a household enjoys a secure roof, every aspect of life stabilises. Health improves, educational outcomes soar, and economic confidence takes root,” he said.
Nga said a city’s success should be measured by the liveability of its neighbourhoods, the quality of public spaces, environmental protection and opportunities for residents, rather than merely its skyline or the scale of construction.
He said housing must cater to people’s needs from early childhood through to elderly care, while urban regeneration should support climate action through energy-efficient technologies and expanded green spaces.
Malaysia was also promoting transit-oriented development and climate-resilient urban renewal as part of its efforts to build more sustainable communities, he also said.
“Policy without execution is merely good intention, vision without action is only a dream,” he added, urging world leaders to translate international commitments into tangible improvements in people’s lives. — Bernama

Title: KL police arrest 18 Taiwanese for posing as Hong Kong police in online scam
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — Police detained 18 Taiwanese nationals suspected of involvement in an online scam syndicate impersonating Hong Kong police after raids on two luxury apartment units here on Thursday.
Dang Wangi police chief ACP Ahmad Azwan Amin Nordin said 17 men and one woman, aged between 19 and 43, were arrested during the 6.35pm raid.
“Police seized 69 mobile phones, five laptops, and two sets of Hong Kong police uniforms,” he said in a statement today.
He added that based on the items recovered, the syndicate is suspected of cheating by posing as Hong Kong police officers and targeting victims in the special administrative region of China.
Ahmad Azwan said initial investigations found the syndicate used local internet access and has likely been operating for about five months.
All suspects have been remanded for four days until November 2 to assist in the investigation under Section 420/511 of the Penal Code.
He also urged members of the public with information about such activities to contact the Dang Wangi District Police Headquarters at 03-26002222 or any nearby police station. — Bernama

Title: Anwar contributes RM200,000 to madrasah in Pondok Lubuk Tapah for repairs
Article:
PASIR MAS, Oct 31 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today presented a contribution of RM200,000 to Madrasah Ar-Rahmaniah Ad-Diniah Pondok Lubuk Tapah here.
The mock cheque, presented under the Kelantan Islamic Educational Institutions Maintenance and Repair Project 2026, was handed over to the madrasah’s chairman, Assoc Prof Datuk Dr Luqman Abdullah.
During the programme, Anwar also spent about 30 minutes visiting Luqman’s residence before performing Maghrib prayers with over 100 local residents.
Also present were Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud and Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat.
Madrasah Ar-Rahmaniah Ad-Diniah Pondok Lubuk Tapah was founded in 1931. — Bernama

Title: RM16b in SARA, STR aid for Malaysians as helping the poor won’t bankrupt the govt, says Anwar
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Oct 31 — The government will not become poor or go bankrupt by helping the less fortunate, as the real threats to the country’s economy are misconduct among leaders, corruption and financial leakages, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
He said providing assistance to low-income groups was the government’s responsibility to ensure that the benefits of national development were shared more widely among the people.
Anwar cited the government’s allocation of RM16 billion this year for the Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) and Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) assistance programmes, alongside increases in civil servants’ salaries and the minimum wage, as measures aimed at improving the people’s well-being.
“No country or government has ever become poor simply by helping the poor,” he said when launching the Kelantan Entrepreneur Revival Scheme here today.
He said a country’s economy could suffer if public wealth was exploited to serve the interests of certain groups, particularly through corruption and greed in the administration.
The Prime Minister stressed that the government must continue to uphold its commitment to helping those in need while maintaining sound financial management and good governance. — Bernama

Title: Anwar unveils additional RM200m grant to support low-income, small-scale entrepreneurs
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Oct 31 — The government has allocated an additional grant of about RM200 million to strengthen the capacity of small-scale entrepreneurs, particularly those from low-income groups, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said small-scale financial assistance could generate meaningful returns for traders if channelled to meet their specific business requirements.
He gave the example of traders who required between RM1,800 and RM5,000 to acquire basic equipment, including refrigerators, to preserve their stock.
“Although the allocation is modest, the benefits go directly to those who need it,” he said when officiating the Kelantan Usahawan Bangkit Scheme here today.
Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud was also present.
Anwar said the federal government was stepping up support for women in Kelantan through entrepreneurship initiatives, recognizing their significant role in the state’s small business sector, including among B40 assistance recipients, and giving them greater opportunities to expand their businesses.
He said women in Kelantan had a strong track record and extensive experience in business, particularly through selling goods at markets, which demonstrated their determination to earn a living.
“That is why I have instructed the Implementation Coordination Unit (ICU) in Kelantan to prioritise assistance programmes for women,” he said.
The Prime Minister said women’s business acumen was evident in Amanah Ikhtiar Malaysia’s nearly 99 per cent loan repayment rate.
On the Kelantan Usahawan Bangkit Scheme, Anwar said more than 4,000 applications had been received from B40 entrepreneurs, with 446 approved so far.
“The scheme provides financial support to small-scale entrepreneurs looking to expand their businesses. So far, more than 4,000 applications have been received from B40 entrepreneurs under Sejati Madani, with 446 approved,” he said.
In another development, the Prime Minister renewed his call for Malaysia to enhance its mastery of emerging technologies, particularly artificial intelligence (AI), digital technology and quantum technology, while upholding religious values, culture and national identity.
He highlighted the importance of keeping pace with global technological developments to ensure the younger generation remained competitive with those in developed nations.
He said the national education system should therefore expand the use of the latest knowledge and technologies, including by introducing the fundamentals of AI at an early stage of schooling.
According to him, national development should be guided by the concept of reaching for the skies while remaining rooted in the earth, which means pursuing advances in knowledge and technology while preserving society’s values and identity.
“This country must progress and master new technologies, including information technology and artificial intelligence, but it must also remain rooted in traditions, a culture grounded in faith, good morals and strong character,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Anwar: Golok River mouth widening project to cut flood risk, talks with Thailand to wrap up within a month
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Oct 31 — Malaysia and Thailand are expected to finalise negotiations on the Golok River mouth widening project within a month to reduce flood risks in Kelantan and southern Thailand.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he had held two rounds of talks with the Thai government, including with his counterpart Anutin Charnvirakul, to expedite the implementation of the project.
He said widening and deepening the river mouth was among the key measures to mitigate the impact of floods affecting areas in both countries.
“I hope to resume negotiations within this month to finalise the matter. There has already been progress between the Malaysian and Thai governments,” he said when speaking at the Kelantan State Entrepreneur Revival Scheme Launch Ceremony here today.
Also present was Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud.
The Prime Minister said close cooperation between the two countries was important to ensure the issue could be resolved effectively, thereby benefiting residents in Kelantan and southern Thailand.
He said good relations with neighbouring countries were important not only in terms of trade, but also in addressing cross-border issues that required joint solutions.
On the flood situation in Kelantan, Anwar gave an assurance that the Federal Government would continue to assist the state in implementing flood mitigation projects, despite the substantial allocations required due to high construction costs.
He said the matter had been discussed with the Kelantan Menteri Besar to facilitate an integrated approach through close cooperation between the state and Federal governments, thereby reducing the impact of floods on the people and the state’s development.
In this regard, Anwar said the government planned to develop the area around the Rantau Panjang Bridge to give the locality a new look through development projects planned in collaboration with the state government.
The Prime Minister stressed that the success of the initiative required firm commitment from both sides, particularly in expediting land acquisition matters.
In this regard, he expressed his appreciation to Kelantan State Secretary Datuk Dr Tengku Mohamed Faziharudean Tengku Feissal for helping to expedite the necessary processes to facilitate the implementation of the development project.
“We are also taking this opportunity to develop the area around the Rantau Panjang Bridge. My thanks to the State Secretary for expediting land acquisition and other related matters so that we can proceed with the project, with the hope of giving Rantau Panjang a new look and bringing progress to the area,” he said.
Anwar said the development was among the government’s efforts to drive socioeconomic growth in the border area, in addition to addressing issues related to the mouth of the Golok River. — Bernama

Title: All relief centres closed in Kedah, Negeri Sembilan as floods subside, Perak evacuees fall to 25
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — Floods in Kedah and Negeri Sembilan have fully subsided, with all three temporary relief centres (PPS) in the two states closed today, while the number of evacuees in Perak has declined.
In Kedah, the last relief centre in Pendang, Dewan Pejabat Penghulu Mukim Bukit Raya, which had been open since last Wednesday, was closed at 10am, allowing all nine evacuees from two families to return home after the floodwaters receded completely.
In Negeri Sembilan, two relief centres in Kuala Pilah, Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Undang Johol and Dewan Orang Ramai Dangi, which housed 87 evacuees from 35 families, were also closed at 4pm today following improved weather and the complete recession of floodwaters.
In Perak, the flood situation has also improved, with the number of evacuees at SK Titi Serong relief centre in Kerian declining to 25 from nine families, compared with 34 people from 12 families this morning.
The Perak State Disaster Management Committee secretariat said in a statement that all evacuees from Taman Aman Sejahtera and Taman Desa Aman 1 had been housed at the centre since Thursday.
Meanwhile, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) forecast rain tonight in Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang and Muallim. — Bernama

Title: No unhealthy readings: Cheras highest at 77 as 47 areas nationwide record moderate API readings this afternoon
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — A total of 47 areas across the country recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at a moderate level as of this evening, while 21 areas recorded good air quality.
According to the Malaysian Air Pollution Index Management System (APIMS) portal, Cheras here recorded the highest moderate API reading at 77, followed by Batu Muda (72). In Selangor, the affected areas include Johan Setia (76), Klang (74), Shah Alam (64), Banting (62), Petaling Jaya (60), and Kuala Selangor (55).
In Johor, the areas are Larkin (73), Kluang (67), Tangkak (62), Pasir Gudang (61), Segamat (56), as well as Pengerang and Kota Tinggi (53 each).
Negeri Sembilan recorded moderate readings in Nilai (69), Seremban (63), and Port Dickson (57), while in Perak, the areas involved are Tasek Ipoh (66), Seri Manjung (56), Pegoh in Ipoh (55), and Taiping (54).
Putrajaya recorded a reading of 65, while in Penang, the areas are Seberang Perai (64), Seberang Jaya (55), and Minden (52).
In Sarawak, seven areas recorded moderate readings: Mukah (64), IPD Serian (59), Kuching (57), Samalaju (56), Sri Aman (55), Sibu (53), and Samarahan (51).
Melaka recorded readings in Bandaraya Melaka (63), Bukit Rambai (62), and Alor Gajah (61), while in Pahang, the area involved is Balok Baru in Kuantan (61).
In Sabah, the areas are Tawau (61), Keningau (55), Kimanis (54), and Sandakan (52), while in Kelantan, they involve Kota Bharu (59) and Tanah Merah (52).
Kedah also recorded moderate readings in Sungai Petani (58) and Kulim Hi-Tech (51), while Kuala Terengganu in Terengganu recorded a reading of 55, and Labuan recorded 52.
Meanwhile, a total of 21 areas recorded good API readings as of this evening, compared to 24 areas in the morning.
API readings between 0 and 50 are categorized as good, 51 to 100 as moderate, 101 to 200 as unhealthy, 201 to 300 as very unhealthy, and 301 and above as hazardous. — Bernama

Title: Perlis PAS announces death of Mata Ayer rep Wan Badariah
Article:
KANGAR, Oct 31 — Mata Ayer assemblywoman Wan Badariah Wan Saad died at Hospital Tuanku Fauziah (HTF) here at 4.26pm today.
Perlis PAS Information chief Mohamad Zahid Ibrahim announced her death in a post on the Perlis PAS Facebook page.
He also extended condolences to her family and urged the public to pray for her soul.
“May Allah shower His blessings upon her soul, forgive her sins and place her among the faithful and the righteous.
“My condolences to all members of her family,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Baby buried in Kapit still hospitalised; mother’s postpartum depression link unconfirmed, says Nancy Shukri
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 31 — The Women, Family and Community Development Ministry (KPWKM) has yet to receive medical confirmation on whether the mother of a baby boy found buried in Kapit recently was suffering from postpartum depression.
Its Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said registered counsellors and hospital medical personnel had important roles to play in identifying the underlying issues faced by the mother.
“We do not know yet, which is why counsellors play a very important role. The Health Ministry also needs to involve the doctors and nurses handling the case.
“I cannot comment beyond what we know so far, as the police are still investigating the case, but our protection team is working with the family and counsellors to determine the actual problem so that they can provide assistance,” she told a press conference after officiating the KPWKM Santuni Kasih Programme here today.
Nancy said discussions on whether the baby would be placed under the care of family members or other suitable parties had yet to be concluded, as both the mother and baby were understood to still be receiving hospital treatment.
She also advised mothers in need of emotional and postnatal health support to seek assistance through the MamaCare initiative, managed by the National Population and Family Development Board (LPPKN).
Earlier, Kapit police chief DSP Rohana Nanu was reported as saying that a baby boy who was still alive was found buried in the ground near a rented house in Jalan Airport, Kapit, on Wednesday.
The baby, who was initially reported to be in critical condition, was rushed to Sibu Hospital for specialist treatment, while the case is being investigated under Section 317 of the Penal Code. — Bernama

Title: Not compulsory, but journalists, your annual check-up could soon come with your press card
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Oct 31 — The Malaysian Media Council (MMC) should explore mechanisms to encourage media practitioners to undergo health screenings during the process of issuing media passes.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the proposed initiative is crucial to ensure that as many as possible of the 12,000 personnel in the media sector benefit and have health issues identified at an early stage.
“I do not want to say to make it compulsory, but we must encourage them. Perhaps the Information Department, before issuing the annual media accreditation card, could ask if they have undergone a medical check-up,” he said today.
He said this in his speech at the launch of the Journalists’ Health Screening Programme with the Cardiac Vascular Sentral Kuala Lumpur (CVSKL) Foundation ahead of the 2026 MMC Annual General Meeting here.
Also present were Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama) Chief Executive Officer Datin Paduka Nur-ul Afida Kamaludin, CVSKL Foundation chairman Tan Sri Rashpal Singh, ECM Libra Foundation chairman Datuk Seri Kalimullah Masheerul Hassan and MMC chairman Tan Sri Nallini Pathmanathan.
Fahmi later told reporters that the proposal for media practitioners to undergo annual health screening has not been set as a prerequisite for media card holders, adding that it would be discussed with the MMC in detail first.
“We will discuss this with the Media Council (and) with all media companies to assess its feasibility; for instance, if this initiative involves facilities in the Klang Valley, it may pose some difficulties for our colleagues in Sabah and Sarawak, or in areas outside the Klang Valley.
“We do not intend to make it compulsory, but we would like to encourage all media teams to undergo health screenings at least once a year. That is our intention,” he said.
On today’s programme, he said the RM1 million initiative, contributed by ECM Libra Foundation to the CVSKL Foundation, aimed to help improve access to preventive healthcare services, particularly for active and former journalists.
“We view problems involving the health of journalists as one of the key issues. These screenings can help identify non-communicable diseases at an early stage, allowing us to provide assistance earlier and help prevent any untoward incidents from occurring,” he added. — Bernama
